```

## Resume

If interrupted, run `/deep-interview` again. The skill reads state from `.omc/state/deep-interview-state.json` and resumes from the last completed round.

## Integration with Autopilot

When autopilot receives a vague input (no file paths, function names, or concrete anchors), it can redirect to deep-interview:

```
User: "autopilot build me a thing"
Autopilot: "Your request is quite open-ended. Would you like to run a deep interview first to clarify requirements?"
  [Yes, interview first] [No, expand directly]
```

If the user chooses interview, autopilot invokes `/deep-interview`. When the interview completes and the user selects "Execute with autopilot", the spec becomes Phase 0 output and autopilot continues from Phase 1 (Planning).

## Approval-Gated Pipeline: deep-interview → omc-plan → pending approval

The recommended refinement path chains clarity and feasibility gates, then stops for explicit execution approval:

```
/deep-interview "vague idea"
  → Socratic Q&A until ambiguity ≤ <resolvedThresholdPercent>
  → Spec written to .omc/specs/deep-interview-{slug}.md
  → User explicitly selects "Refine with omc-plan consensus"
  → Skill("oh-my-claudecode:plan") with --consensus --direct (spec as input, skip interview)
    → Planner creates implementation plan from spec
    → Architect reviews for architectural soundness
    → Critic validates quality and testability
    → Loop until consensus (max 5 iterations)
    → Consensus plan written to .omc/plans/
  → Stop with the consensus plan marked pending approval
  → Only a separate explicit execution approval may invoke team/ralph/autopilot
```

**The omc-plan skill receives the spec with `--consensus --direct` flags** because the deep interview already did the requirements gathering. The `--direct` flag (supported by the omc-plan skill, which ralplan aliases) skips the interview phase and goes straight to Planner → Architect → Critic consensus. The consensus plan includes:
- RALPLAN-DR summary (Principles, Decision Drivers, Options)
- ADR (Decision, Drivers, Alternatives, Why chosen, Consequences)
- Testable acceptance criteria (inherited from deep-interview spec)
- Implementation steps with file references

**Execution is a separate approval-gated step.** The deep-interview and omc-plan skills must not auto-invoke autopilot, team, ralph, or any other execution skill merely because a spec or plan exists.

## Integration with Ralplan Gate

The ralplan pre-execution gate already redirects vague prompts to planning. Deep interview can serve as an alternative redirect target for prompts that are too vague even for ralplan:

```
Vague prompt → ralplan gate → deep-interview (if extremely vague) → omc-plan (with clear spec) → pending approval → explicitly approved execution
```

## Brownfield vs Greenfield Weights

| Dimension | Greenfield | Brownfield |
|-----------|-----------|------------|
| Goal Clarity | 40% | 35% |
| Constraint Clarity | 30% | 25% |
| Success Criteria | 30% | 25% |
| Context Clarity | N/A | 15% |

Brownfield adds Context Clarity because modifying existing code safely requires understanding the system being changed.

## Challenge Agent Modes

| Mode | Activates | Purpose | Prompt Injection |
|------|-----------|---------|-----------------|
| Contrarian | Round 4+ | Challenge assumptions | "What if the opposite were true?" |
| Simplifier | Round 6+ | Remove complexity | "What's the simplest version?" |
| Ontologist | Round 8+ (if ambiguity > 0.3) | Find essence | "What IS this, really?" |

Each mode is used exactly once, then normal Socratic questioning resumes. Modes are tracked in state to prevent repetition.

## Ambiguity Score Interpretation

| Score Range | Meaning | Action |
|-------------|---------|--------|
| 0.0 - 0.1 | Crystal clear | Proceed immediately |
| At or below the resolved threshold | Clear enough | Proceed |
| Above the resolved threshold with minor gaps | Some gaps | Continue interviewing |
| Moderate ambiguity | Significant gaps | Focus on weakest dimensions |
| High ambiguity | Very unclear | May need reframing (Ontologist) |
| Extreme ambiguity | Almost nothing known | Early stages, keep going |

questions.question:
Round 1 | Topic: Accessibility & devices | Targeting: Constraints | Why now: phone-first vs desktop-first decides the layout of every other screen | Ambiguity: ~72%

Where will people mostly use this app?

Cause → effect:
• Phone-first: designed for a phone at the restaurant table, then stretched to fill bigger screens. Effect: big tap targets, one column, bottom navigation bar on phones and a sidebar on computers. Perfect for splitting a bill on the spot. On a big monitor, some space is left empty.
• Desktop-first: designed for a computer, then squeezed onto phones. Effect: side-by-side panels (e.g. bill on the left, results on the right) and wide tables of balances. Great at home, but more cramped and fiddly at the table.
• Equal priority: two fully separate layouts tuned for each. Effect: best on both, but roughly double the design and testing work.

What should you see right after logging in, and how do you get around?

How accessible should the app be?

Cause → effect:
• Meet the WCAG 2.2 AA standard (the common legal and industry benchmark):
  - Everything works with the keyboard alone (Tab, Enter, Esc), with a visible focus outline.
  - Text contrast is at least 4.5:1, in both light and dark mode.
  - Every field has a label, and screen readers announce errors and results.
  - Red/green is never the only signal; there's always a "+" / "−" or "owes" / "is owed" too.
  - It still works at 200% browser zoom.
  - Automated accessibility checks run with the tests.
  Effect: usable by people with low vision, colour blindness or no mouse, and it's checkable. A bit more care on every screen.
• Basics only: labels, keyboard access and decent contrast, with no formal target or automated checks. Effect: less work, but no clear pass/fail standard.
• No specific effort: fastest to build, but some people won't be able to use it, and there's nothing to test against.

Ambiguity sits at 30%, so next I'll tackle feedback & success criteria—defining how the app confirms actions and handles loading/empty states.

questions.question:
Round 9 | Topic: Feedback & states | Targeting: Success criteria | Why now: how the app confirms success, shows waiting and handles empty screens is still undefined, so none of it can be tested | Ambiguity: 30%

How should the app give feedback?

Cause → effect:
• Full feedback set:
  - Success: a small message in the corner ("Bill saved", "Payment recorded") that disappears after 5 seconds and is also read out by screen readers.
  - Saving: the button shows "Saving…" and is disabled until the save finishes, so a double-click can't save the same bill twice.
  - Loading: grey placeholder shapes while a page loads.
  - Empty screens: a short explanation plus the next step ("No groups yet. Create one to start splitting with friends." [Create group]).
  - Deletes and leaving: a pop-up confirmation box, with the dangerous button in red.
  Effect: you always know what happened, and duplicate saves are impossible.
• Messages on the page only: success text appears near the form, and there are no corner messages or loading placeholders. Effect: simpler, but easy to miss, and double-clicks aren't guarded.
• Minimal: just errors (already in the spec) and delete confirmations. Effect: least work, but the app feels silent and uncertain.

Round 10 | Topic: Bill entry + Results | Targeting: Constraints | Why now: the spec says letters are rejected, but not whether "1,000.50" (with a comma) is allowed, or how amounts are displayed | Ambiguity: 25.3%

How should numbers be typed and shown, and in what language?

Cause → effect:
• English, standard number style:
  - Shown with a thousands comma and a dot for decimals: "1,000,000.00".
  - Currency symbol before the amount, with a space for letter symbols: "$12.50", "€12.50", "Rs 400.00", "CHF 12.00".
  - Typing accepts both "1000.50" and "1,000.50" (commas are ignored), but not "1.000,50" (European style), which shows the normal field message.
  - All text is in English.
  Effect: one clear format, friendly typing, and easy to test.
• No commas when typing: only "1000.50" is accepted, and amounts are still shown with commas. Effect: stricter, and pasting "1,000.50" from a receipt gives an error.
• Follow the device's region: e.g. a German computer shows "1.000,50". Effect: feels native everywhere, but there are many formats to support and test, and it's confusing when friends in different regions see different formats.

questions.question:
Round 11 | Topic: Feedback & states | Targeting: Success criteria | Why now: it's still undefined what happens to a half-filled bill when you click away | Ambiguity: 21.3%

You've typed 8 items and haven't saved, then click "Groups" in the sidebar. What should happen?

Cause → effect:
• Warn before leaving: a dialog asks "You have unsaved changes. Leave without saving?" with [Stay] and [Leave] (Leave in red). The same applies when closing the browser tab. Effect: you never lose work by accident. Nothing is stored that you didn't choose to save.
• Auto-save a draft: the half-filled bill is kept as a draft in your account and appears as "Draft" in your history until you finish or discard it. Effect: you can come back later, but drafts are a whole new feature to build and test, and drafts of group bills could confuse other members.
• No warning: the page just changes and the typing is lost. Effect: simplest, but frustrating after typing a long receipt.

## Acceptance Criteria
### Accounts (AC-A)
input.new_string:
## Frontend Design (v2.6)

Decided in the frontend interview (11 rounds, final ambiguity 18.4%).

### Devices and layout
- **Desktop-first:** designed for a computer screen first, then adapted to phones. It must still be fully usable on a phone, at widths down to 360 px, with no sideways scrolling of the page.
- **Navigation:** a **left sidebar** with Dashboard, Solo bills, Groups and Account is always visible on wide screens. On narrow screens (phones) it folds into a menu button at the top.

### Screens
- **Dashboard (first screen after login):**
  - A money summary: "You owe" and "You're owed", one line **per currency**, because groups can use different currencies and amounts are never added across currencies.
  - Your groups, each with your balance in that group.
  - Your latest solo bills.
  - Quick buttons: "New solo bill" and "New group bill".
- **Bill form** (solo, equal split, itemized split):
  - Items are entered as rows.
  - Tax, other charges and tip each have a % / amount switch next to the field.
  - The "tip on" option (food only / food + tax) appears only when the tip is a %.
  - **Itemized bills:** each item row has a **multi-select dropdown** listing the bill's participants with tick boxes. When closed, it shows the chosen names (e.g. "Ali, Sara, Omar"). An empty selection shows "Choose who shared this item".
  - **Payer:** chosen from a dropdown that lists only ticked participants.
- **Results:** shown **below the form** on every screen size.
  - After Calculate, the page scrolls down to them.
  - They list subtotal, tax, other charges, tip and total, then (for group bills) each person's share, with "+1 cent" marked on people who pay an extra cent.
  - Before the first Calculate, the area reads "Press Calculate to see results".
  - Changing any input hides the result again.
- **Group page (balances first):**
  - Top: each member's balance (e.g. "+13.00 is owed", "−13.00 owes") and the suggested payments. Each suggestion has a **"Record this payment"** button that opens the settle-up form pre-filled with that payer, receiver and amount, for the user to confirm or adjust.
  - An "Add bill" button is always visible at the top.
  - Tabs below: **Bills · Settle-ups · Members · Activity**. The invite code (with Copy) and Removed members (with Restore) are on the Members tab.
- **Account page:** log out, appearance setting, and password reset.

### Look and feel
- **Clean and calm:** lots of white space, a soft grey page background, white rounded cards, one accent color for buttons, links and highlights, and clear readable fonts.
- **Money colors:** amounts you owe are red, and amounts owed to you are green. Colour is never the only signal: "+" / "−" and "owes" / "is owed" are always shown too.
- **Appearance:** light or dark mode **follows the device** by default. A setting in Account (Device / Light / Dark) overrides it and is remembered for the account. Both themes meet the contrast rules below.

### Numbers and language
- All text is in **English**.
- Amounts are shown with a thousands comma and 2 decimals: "1,000,000.00".
- The currency symbol goes before the amount: "$12.50", "€12.50". Symbols made of letters get a space: "Rs 400.00", "CHF 12.00", "AED 5.00", and the same for custom symbols such as "kr 30.00".
- **Typing amounts:** "1000.50" and "1,000.50" are both accepted (commas are ignored). European style "1.000,50" and misplaced commas are rejected with the field's normal message. Percent fields accept "12.5" and "12.5%".

### Feedback and states
- **Success messages:** a short message in the corner ("Bill saved", "Payment recorded", "Member removed") that disappears after 5 seconds and is announced to screen readers.
- **Saving:** the button shows "Saving…" and is disabled until the save finishes, so a double-click never saves twice.
- **Loading:** grey placeholder shapes while a page's data loads.
- **Empty screens:** a short explanation plus the next step, e.g. "No groups yet. Create one to start splitting with friends." [Create group]. The same applies to no solo bills, no group bills and no activity.
- **Confirmations:** deleting, removing a member, leaving and closing out a group use a pop-up dialog, with the dangerous button in red and Cancel/Stay as the safe default.
- **Unsaved changes:** leaving a bill form with unsaved changes (sidebar link, back button, other link) asks "You have unsaved changes. Leave without saving?" [Stay] [Leave]. Closing or reloading the tab triggers the browser's own "Leave site?" prompt. No drafts are stored.

### Accessibility (best practice: WCAG 2.2 AA)
- **Keyboard:** everything works with the keyboard alone (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Esc, arrow keys in dropdowns), with a clearly visible focus outline. Dialogs keep focus inside and close with Esc.
- **Contrast:** at least 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for controls and focus outlines, in both light and dark mode.
- **Screen readers:** every field has a visible label. Errors are linked to their field and announced. Results and success messages are announced.
- **Zoom:** usable at 200% browser zoom.
- **Touch targets:** at least 24×24 px.
- **Testing:** automated accessibility checks (axe) run as part of `npm test` and must report no violations.

## Acceptance Criteria
### Frontend (AC-F)
- [ ] Given a screen 1280 px wide, then the sidebar is always visible. Given a screen 375 px wide, then it's replaced by a menu button, and every page fits with no sideways page scrolling.
- [ ] Given I log in, then I land on the Dashboard, showing per-currency "You owe" / "You're owed" lines, my groups with my balance in each, my latest solo bills, and "New solo bill" / "New group bill" buttons.
- [ ] Given I'm in groups using $ and Rs, then the Dashboard shows separate totals for $ and Rs, never one combined number.
- [ ] Given an itemized bill, when I open an item's people dropdown, then it lists only the bill's participants with tick boxes. When closed, it shows the ticked names.
- [ ] Given I press Calculate with valid inputs, then the results appear below the form and the page scrolls to them. Given I change any input, then the results area goes back to "Press Calculate to see results".
- [ ] Given I open a group, then balances and suggested payments are at the top, followed by the tabs Bills, Settle-ups, Members and Activity.
- [ ] Given I press "Record this payment" on "Sara pays Ali 13.00", then the settle-up form opens pre-filled with Sara → Ali, 13.00, and nothing is saved until I confirm.
- [ ] Given my device is in dark mode and the appearance setting is "Device", then the app is dark. Given I choose "Light", then it stays light after logging out and back in.

## Acceptance Criteria
### Accounts (AC-A)
input.new_string:
## Frontend Design (v2.6)

Decided in the frontend interview (11 rounds, final ambiguity 18.4%).

### Devices and layout
- **Desktop-first:** designed for a computer screen first, then adapted to phones. It must still be fully usable on a phone, at widths down to 360 px, with no sideways scrolling of the page.
- **Navigation:** a **left sidebar** with Dashboard, Solo bills, Groups and Account is always visible on wide screens. On narrow screens (phones) it folds into a menu button at the top.

### Screens
- **Dashboard (first screen after login):**
  - A money summary: "You owe" and "You're owed", one line **per currency**, because groups can use different currencies and amounts are never added across currencies.
  - Your groups, each with your balance in that group.
  - Your latest solo bills.
  - Quick buttons: "New solo bill" and "New group bill".
- **Bill form** (solo, equal split, itemized split):
  - Items are entered as rows.
  - Tax, other charges and tip each have a % / amount switch next to the field.
  - The "tip on" option (food only / food + tax) appears only when the tip is a %.
  - **Itemized bills:** each item row has a **multi-select dropdown** listing the bill's participants with tick boxes. When closed, it shows the chosen names (e.g. "Ali, Sara, Omar"). An empty selection shows "Choose who shared this item".
  - **Payer:** chosen from a dropdown that lists only ticked participants.
- **Results:** shown **below the form** on every screen size.
  - After Calculate, the page scrolls down to them.
  - They list subtotal, tax, other charges, tip and total, then (for group bills) each person's share, with "+1 cent" marked on people who pay an extra cent.
  - Before the first Calculate, the area reads "Press Calculate to see results".
  - Changing any input hides the result again.
- **Group page (balances first):**
  - Top: each member's balance (e.g. "+13.00 is owed", "−13.00 owes") and the suggested payments. Each suggestion has a **"Record this payment"** button that opens the settle-up form pre-filled with that payer, receiver and amount, for the user to confirm or adjust.
  - An "Add bill" button is always visible at the top.
  - Tabs below: **Bills · Settle-ups · Members · Activity**. The invite code (with Copy) and Removed members (with Restore) are on the Members tab.
- **Account page:** log out, appearance setting, and password reset.

### Look and feel
- **Clean and calm:** lots of white space, a soft grey page background, white rounded cards, one accent color for buttons, links and highlights, and clear readable fonts.
- **Money colors:** amounts you owe are red, and amounts owed to you are green. Colour is never the only signal: "+" / "−" and "owes" / "is owed" are always shown too.
- **Appearance:** light or dark mode **follows the device** by default. A setting in Account (Device / Light / Dark) overrides it and is remembered for the account. Both themes meet the contrast rules below.

### Numbers and language
- All text is in **English**.
- Amounts are shown with a thousands comma and 2 decimals: "1,000,000.00".
- The currency symbol goes before the amount: "$12.50", "€12.50". Symbols made of letters get a space: "Rs 400.00", "CHF 12.00", "AED 5.00", and the same for custom symbols such as "kr 30.00".
- **Typing amounts:** "1000.50" and "1,000.50" are both accepted (commas are ignored). European style "1.000,50" and misplaced commas are rejected with the field's normal message. Percent fields accept "12.5" and "12.5%".

### Feedback and states
- **Success messages:** a short message in the corner ("Bill saved", "Payment recorded", "Member removed") that disappears after 5 seconds and is announced to screen readers.
- **Saving:** the button shows "Saving…" and is disabled until the save finishes, so a double-click never saves twice.
- **Loading:** grey placeholder shapes while a page's data loads.
- **Empty screens:** a short explanation plus the next step, e.g. "No groups yet. Create one to start splitting with friends." [Create group]. The same applies to no solo bills, no group bills and no activity.
- **Confirmations:** deleting, removing a member, leaving and closing out a group use a pop-up dialog, with the dangerous button in red and Cancel/Stay as the safe default.
- **Unsaved changes:** leaving a bill form with unsaved changes (sidebar link, back button, other link) asks "You have unsaved changes. Leave without saving?" [Stay] [Leave]. Closing or reloading the tab triggers the browser's own "Leave site?" prompt. No drafts are stored.

### Accessibility (best practice: WCAG 2.2 AA)
- **Keyboard:** everything works with the keyboard alone (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Esc, arrow keys in dropdowns), with a clearly visible focus outline. Dialogs keep focus inside and close with Esc.
- **Contrast:** at least 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for controls and focus outlines, in both light and dark mode.
- **Screen readers:** every field has a visible label. Errors are linked to their field and announced. Results and success messages are announced.
- **Zoom:** usable at 200% browser zoom.
- **Touch targets:** at least 24×24 px.
- **Testing:** automated accessibility checks (axe) run as part of `npm test` and must report no violations.

## Acceptance Criteria
### Frontend (AC-F)
- [ ] Given a screen 1280 px wide, then the sidebar is always visible. Given a screen 375 px wide, then it's replaced by a menu button, and every page fits with no sideways page scrolling.
- [ ] Given I log in, then I land on the Dashboard, showing per-currency "You owe" / "You're owed" lines, my groups with my balance in each, my latest solo bills, and "New solo bill" / "New group bill" buttons.
- [ ] Given I'm in groups using $ and Rs, then the Dashboard shows separate totals for $ and Rs, never one combined number.
- [ ] Given an itemized bill, when I open an item's people dropdown, then it lists only the bill's participants with tick boxes. When closed, it shows the ticked names.
- [ ] Given I press Calculate with valid inputs, then the results appear below the form and the page scrolls to them. Given I change any input, then the results area goes back to "Press Calculate to see results".
- [ ] Given I open a group, then balances and suggested payments are at the top, followed by the tabs Bills, Settle-ups, Members and Activity.
- [ ] Given I press "Record this payment" on "Sara pays Ali 13.00", then the settle-up form opens pre-filled with Sara → Ali, 13.00, and nothing is saved until I confirm.
- [ ] Given my device is in dark mode and the appearance setting is "Device", then the app is dark. Given I choose "Light", then it stays light after logging out and back in.
- [ ] Given amounts of 1234567.5 and 400 in Rs, then they're shown as "1,234,567.50" and "Rs 400.00".
- [ ] Given I type "1,000.50" in a money field, then it's accepted as 1000.50. Given I type "1.000,50", then the field's normal message is shown.
- [ ] Given I save a bill, then the Save button shows "Saving…" and is disabled until the save finishes, a "Bill saved" message appears and disappears after 5 seconds, and double-clicking Save creates only one bill.
- [ ] Given I have no groups, then the Groups page shows "No groups yet. Create one to start splitting with friends." with a Create group button.
- [ ] Given I've changed a bill form without saving, when I click a sidebar link, then I'm asked "You have unsaved changes. Leave without saving?". Stay keeps everything, and Leave discards the changes.
- [ ] Given I use only the keyboard, then I can sign up, create a group, add a bill, calculate, save and record a settle-up, with a visible focus outline at every step.
- [ ] Given any page in light or dark mode, then automated accessibility checks report no WCAG 2.2 AA violations, and text contrast is at least 4.5:1.
- [ ] Given 200% browser zoom, then every page is still usable with no lost content or functions.

### Accounts (AC-A)

# Jobs to Be Done

Why people use the Bill Splitting Calculator. Each job is something the person needs to get done whether or not this app exists, so no job mentions the app, its screens or its buttons. Each job names the role it belongs to (see [app-roles.md](app-roles.md)), and every story in [user-stories.md](user-stories.md) names the job it serves.

## Solo diner

**J1. Know exactly what I owe**
When I've finished a meal or a purchase on my own and the bill adds tax, extra fees and a tip, I want to know the exact amount to pay, to the cent, so I can pay the right amount without doing the maths in my head.
- Role: Solo diner

**J2. Keep a record of my own spending**
When I look back at what I've spent on meals and purchases, I want an accurate record of each past bill that I can correct or remove, so I can keep track of my spending and trust the numbers.
- Role: Solo diner

## Group member

**J3. Share a bill evenly**
When a group of us shares one bill and we agree to split it evenly, I want each person's share worked out so that the shares add up to exactly the bill, so I can make sure nobody pays a cent too much or too little.
- Role: Group member

**J4. Pay for what each person had**
When a group of us orders different things, including dishes some of us share, I want each person to pay for what they had plus a fair part of the tax, fees and tip, so I can make the split fair to people who ordered less.
- Role: Group member

**J5. Charge only the people who were there**
When one friend pays for an outing that only some of our friend group joined, I want to note who paid and who took part, so I can make sure only the people who were there owe a share and the person who paid gets it back.
- Role: Group member

**J6. Know who owes whom overall**
When my friends and I share costs again and again over weeks or months, I want to know at any moment what each person owes or is owed in total, and the fewest payments that would square everyone up, so I can settle debts without long lists of back-and-forth payments.
- Role: Group member

**J7. Count repayments**
When one friend pays another back, I want that repayment taken off what they owed, even if they pay back more than they owed, so I can keep everyone's running totals correct.
- Role: Group member

**J8. Include friends who don't keep records**
When some friends in our circle don't keep their own records of shared costs, I want to include them in our shared costs from the start and let them take over their own part whenever they choose to, so I can keep everyone's history complete.
- Role: Group member

**J9. See who changed what**
When anyone in our group adds, changes or removes a shared cost or a repayment, I want to see who did it, when, and what changed, so I can trust the totals and sort out disagreements.
- Role: Group member

**J10. Keep history right when people leave or come back**
When someone leaves our circle of friends, or comes back later, I want their past share to stay exactly as it was and their access to our shared records to end or return with them, so I can keep our history correct and keep it private to the people currently in the group.
- Role: Group member

**J11. Close out a group for good**
When I'm the last person still keeping a group's shared records and we're finished with them, I want to close them out completely, so I can leave nothing behind.
- Role: Group member

## Solo diner and Group member

**J12. Keep my money records private**
When I keep records of what I've spent, paid or am owed, I want only me, or only the friends a record concerns, to be able to see or change them, so I can trust that nobody else reads or alters my financial details.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J13. Get back in without help**
When I forget the secret I use to protect my records, I want a way to regain access that doesn't depend on anyone else, so I can make sure I never lose my history.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J14. Catch mistakes before relying on a figure**
When I'm working out money amounts and I make a typing mistake or enter something impossible, I want the mistake caught and clearly explained before I rely on the result, so I can never pay or charge someone the wrong amount.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J15. See amounts in my own currency**
When I pay in a particular currency, I want amounts shown with that currency's symbol and kept in one currency throughout, so I can read every figure without confusion.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J16. Use the browser I already have**
When I need to work out or check a bill, I want to do it in whichever common, up-to-date web browser I already use, so I can avoid installing or buying anything extra.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

- Role: Host

- Role: Host

## Screens, appearance and accessibility

### US-33 See my money at a glance on the Dashboard
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** a home screen that sums up what I owe and what I'm owed, **so that** I know where I stand the moment I log in.
- **Job:** J20 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I log in, then I land on the Dashboard.
2. Given I'm in groups, then the Dashboard shows "You owe" and "You're owed" totals across all my groups, one line per currency.
3. Given I'm in one group using $ and another using Rs, then the Dashboard shows separate $ and Rs totals, never one combined number.
4. Given I'm in groups, then each group is listed with my own balance in it, and clicking a group opens its page.
5. Given I have solo bills, then my latest solo bills are listed, newest first.
6. Given the Dashboard, then "New solo bill" and "New group bill" buttons are visible.
7. Given I have no groups and no solo bills, then each section shows a short explanation and a button for the next step instead of an empty space.
8. Given every balance across my groups is 0.00, then the Dashboard says I owe nothing and am owed nothing.

### US-34 Find my way on a computer or a phone
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** clear navigation that works on a big screen and a small one, **so that** I can use whichever device I have with me.
- **Job:** J16 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a screen 1280 px wide, then a left sidebar with Dashboard, Solo bills, Groups and Account is always visible.
2. Given a screen 375 px wide, then the sidebar is replaced by a menu button at the top, which opens the same four links.
3. Given any page at any width from 360 px up, then all content fits with no sideways scrolling of the page.
4. Given I'm on a page, then its sidebar or menu link is highlighted, so I can see where I am.
5. Given the Account page, then it shows my username, the appearance setting and a Log out button.

### US-35 Choose light or dark appearance
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** the app to be light or dark to suit my surroundings, **so that** figures are comfortable to read day or night.
- **Job:** J21 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given the appearance setting is "Device" (the default) and my device is in dark mode, then the app is dark. When the device switches to light mode, the app follows.
2. Given I choose "Light" or "Dark" on the Account page, then the app uses that look regardless of my device setting.
3. Given I chose "Dark", when I log out and back in (on any computer), then the app is still dark, because the choice is saved with my account.
4. Given either theme, then all text has at least 4.5:1 contrast, and owed / owes amounts keep their "+" / "−" and words as well as colour.

### US-36 Use the app with a keyboard, screen reader or zoom
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** every feature to work without a mouse, with a screen reader and at large text sizes, **so that** I can manage my money on my own.
- **Job:** J22 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I use only the keyboard, then I can sign up, log in, create a group, add members, add an itemized bill (including choosing people in the item dropdowns), calculate, save, record a settle-up and log out, with a clearly visible focus outline at every step.
2. Given a confirmation dialog is open, then keyboard focus stays inside it, and Esc closes it the same way as Cancel.
3. Given a screen reader, then every field has a label, each error is read out with its field, and new results and success messages are announced.
4. Given 200% browser zoom, then every page is still usable with no lost content or functions.
5. Given any button, link or tick box, then its touch or click area is at least 24×24 px.
6. Given any page in light or dark mode, when the automated accessibility checks run as part of `npm test`, then they report no WCAG 2.2 AA violations.

### US-37 Know what happened after every action
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** clear signs when something is saving, saved, loading or empty, **so that** I'm never unsure whether it worked and never save something twice.
- **Job:** J14 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I save a bill, record a payment or remove a member, then a short corner message appears ("Bill saved", "Payment recorded", "Member removed"), disappears after 5 seconds, and is announced by screen readers.
2. Given I press Save, then the button shows "Saving…" and is disabled until the save finishes.
3. Given I double-click Save, then only one bill is created.
4. Given a page is loading its data, then grey placeholder shapes are shown until the content appears.
5. Given I have no groups, then the Groups page shows "No groups yet. Create one to start splitting with friends." with a Create group button. Empty solo-bill, group-bill and activity lists likewise explain what to do next.
6. Given I press Delete, Remove member, Leave or close out a group, then a pop-up asks me to confirm. The dangerous button is red, and Cancel or Stay is the safe default.

### US-38 Don't lose unsaved changes by accident
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** a warning before I leave a bill I haven't saved, **so that** I don't lose a long receipt I've typed in.
- **Job:** J14 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I've changed a bill form without saving, when I click a sidebar link, the back button or any other link, then I'm asked "You have unsaved changes. Leave without saving?" with Stay and Leave.
2. Given that question, when I press Stay, then I stay on the form with everything I typed.
3. Given that question, when I press Leave, then I go to the other page and the changes are discarded. Nothing is saved as a draft.
4. Given I've changed a bill form without saving, when I close or reload the browser tab, then the browser's own "Leave site?" prompt appears.
5. Given I haven't changed anything, or I've just saved, when I leave the form, then no warning appears.

# App Roles

Who uses the Bill Splitting Calculator. Each role is a different kind of person with different needs. Jobs are in [jobs-to-be-done.md](jobs-to-be-done.md), and stories are in [user-stories.md](user-stories.md).

## Solo diner

A **Solo diner** is someone who eats out, orders in or shops on their own and pays their own bill. They want to know the exact amount to pay, including tax, any other charges (such as a service, delivery or table fee) and tip, and they want a private record of what they've spent.

They can:
- create an account with a username and password, receive a one-time recovery code, log in, log out, and reset a forgotten password with that code
- enter a bill's items, tax, other charges and tip, each of tax, other charges and tip as a % or an amount, and choose whether a % tip is on the food only or on the food + tax
- pick the bill's currency symbol, press Calculate and see the subtotal, tax, other charges, tip and total, exact to the cent
- save the bill to their personal history, then reopen, edit or delete saved bills

They must never:
- see another person's solo bills, or have their own solo bills seen or changed by anyone else, even by typing a page address directly
- change a solo bill's currency once that bill has been saved
- be shown a wrong, stale or broken result (such as NaN, Infinity or "undefined") for any input

## Group member

A **Group member** belongs to one or more lasting groups of friends who share costs again and again: meals, trips, groceries. Every member has equal rights; there is no admin or organizer. A bill may involve the whole group or only the members who took part, and one person usually pays the bill for everyone. They want to know, at any time, who owes whom across all the group's bills, and the fewest payments needed to settle up.

They can:
- create a group with a name and a currency, and add friends to it by name, even friends who never create an account
- view the group's invite code and copy it, and use an invite code to join a group by claiming their name, or to rejoin a group they were removed from
- record a group bill: choose who took part, who paid (one of the people who took part) and whether to split it equally or by items, with shared items split between the people who had them
- see every member's running balance and the suggested payments to settle up, and record settle-ups (repayments) of any valid amount
- add, edit or delete any group bill or settle-up, and see every change in the group's activity log
- remove a member whose balance is 0.00, leave the group when their own balance is 0.00, and restore removed members
- as the last member with an account, leave after a warning, which permanently deletes the group

They must never:
- see or open a group they don't belong to, including a group they've been removed from
- remove another member, or leave themselves, while that member's balance isn't 0.00. The one exception is the last member with an account leaving, which deletes the group after a warning.
- record a bill whose payer isn't one of the people who took part in it
- edit or delete a bill or settle-up that includes a removed member, until that member is restored
- change the group's currency after the group is created
- create a brand-new member by entering an invite code; only current members add new names

## Host

A **Host** is someone who installs and runs their own copy of the app. This is either a reviewer checking the project on their own computer, or someone running it on a server so their friends can use it. They don't need to know how the app works inside, but they need it to start reliably by following the README, with nothing to buy or sign up for.

They can:
- install it with only free software (Node.js LTS and Docker), start its own PostgreSQL database container, and start the app by following the README
- run it on a server, configured only through settings the app owns (port, `DATABASE_URL`, session secret), with a self-hosted PostgreSQL database
- run all of the app's automated tests with one command, against a separate test database that never touches real data

They must never:
- need a paid account, an API key or any third-party cloud or paid service to install, run, test or deploy the app. The PostgreSQL database is self-hosted and runs in their own container.
- lose saved data by restarting the app or the database container

## How the roles differ

| Need | Solo diner | Group member | Host |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main question | "What do I owe for this bill?" | "Who owes whom across all our bills?" | "Does it run and work as promised?" |
| Who sees the data | Only them | Only the group's current members | Doesn't use bill data |
| Splitting | None, one person pays everything | Equal or by items, among the people who took part | — |
| Payer and balances | Not needed | One payer per bill, running balances, settle-ups | — |
| Changing records | Their own bills only | Any group bill or settle-up, with every change logged | — |
| Account needed | Yes | Yes, to log in; friends without accounts appear as name-only members | No app account needed to install or run |

## Notes

- **One person can hold several roles.** The same account can keep solo bills (Solo diner) and belong to groups (Group member).
- **Name-only members are not a role.** Friends who never sign up exist only as names inside a group. They can be chosen as a participant, and as the payer of bills they took part in, but they never use the app themselves unless they later create an account and claim their name.

## Screens, appearance and accessibility

### US-33 See my money at a glance on the Dashboard
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** a home screen that sums up what I owe and what I'm owed, **so that** I know where I stand the moment I log in.
- **Job:** J20 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I log in, then I land on the Dashboard.
2. Given I'm in groups, then the Dashboard shows "You owe" and "You're owed" totals across all my groups, one line per currency.
3. Given I'm in one group using $ and another using Rs, then the Dashboard shows separate $ and Rs totals, never one combined number.
4. Given I'm in groups, then each group is listed with my own balance in it, and clicking a group opens its page.
5. Given I have solo bills, then my latest solo bills are listed, newest first.
6. Given the Dashboard, then "New solo bill" and "New group bill" buttons are visible.
7. Given I have no groups and no solo bills, then each section shows a short explanation and a button for the next step instead of an empty space.
8. Given every balance across my groups is 0.00, then the Dashboard says I owe nothing and am owed nothing.

### US-34 Find my way on a computer or a phone
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** clear navigation that works on a big screen and a small one, **so that** I can use whichever device I have with me.
- **Job:** J16 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a screen 1280 px wide, then a left sidebar with Dashboard, Solo bills, Groups and Account is always visible.
2. Given a screen 375 px wide, then the sidebar is replaced by a menu button at the top, which opens the same four links.
3. Given any page at any width from 360 px up, then all content fits with no sideways scrolling of the page.
4. Given I'm on a page, then its sidebar or menu link is highlighted, so I can see where I am.
5. Given the Account page, then it shows my username, the appearance setting and a Log out button.

### US-35 Choose light or dark appearance
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** the app to be light or dark to suit my surroundings, **so that** figures are comfortable to read day or night.
- **Job:** J21 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given the appearance setting is "Device" (the default) and my device is in dark mode, then the app is dark. When the device switches to light mode, the app follows.
2. Given I choose "Light" or "Dark" on the Account page, then the app uses that look regardless of my device setting.
3. Given I chose "Dark", when I log out and back in (on any computer), then the app is still dark, because the choice is saved with my account.
4. Given either theme, then all text has at least 4.5:1 contrast, and owed / owes amounts keep their "+" / "−" and words as well as colour.

### US-36 Use the app with a keyboard, screen reader or zoom
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** every feature to work without a mouse, with a screen reader and at large text sizes, **so that** I can manage my money on my own.
- **Job:** J22 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I use only the keyboard, then I can sign up, log in, create a group, add members, add an itemized bill (including choosing people in the item dropdowns), calculate, save, record a settle-up and log out, with a clearly visible focus outline at every step.
2. Given a confirmation dialog is open, then keyboard focus stays inside it, and Esc closes it the same way as Cancel.
3. Given a screen reader, then every field has a label, each error is read out with its field, and new results and success messages are announced.
4. Given 200% browser zoom, then every page is still usable with no lost content or functions.
5. Given any button, link or tick box, then its touch or click area is at least 24×24 px.
6. Given any page in light or dark mode, when the automated accessibility checks run as part of `npm test`, then they report no WCAG 2.2 AA violations.

### US-37 Know what happened after every action
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** clear signs when something is saving, saved, loading or empty, **so that** I'm never unsure whether it worked and never save something twice.
- **Job:** J14 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I save a bill, record a payment or remove a member, then a short corner message appears ("Bill saved", "Payment recorded", "Member removed"), disappears after 5 seconds, and is announced by screen readers.
2. Given I press Save, then the button shows "Saving…" and is disabled until the save finishes.
3. Given I double-click Save, then only one bill is created.
4. Given a page is loading its data, then grey placeholder shapes are shown until the content appears.
5. Given I have no groups, then the Groups page shows "No groups yet. Create one to start splitting with friends." with a Create group button. Empty solo-bill, group-bill and activity lists likewise explain what to do next.
6. Given I press Delete, Remove member, Leave or close out a group, then a pop-up asks me to confirm. The dangerous button is red, and Cancel or Stay is the safe default.

### US-38 Don't lose unsaved changes by accident
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** a warning before I leave a bill I haven't saved, **so that** I don't lose a long receipt I've typed in.
- **Job:** J14 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I've changed a bill form without saving, when I click a sidebar link, the back button or any other link, then I'm asked "You have unsaved changes. Leave without saving?" with Stay and Leave.
2. Given that question, when I press Stay, then I stay on the form with everything I typed.
3. Given that question, when I press Leave, then I go to the other page and the changes are discarded. Nothing is saved as a draft.
4. Given I've changed a bill form without saving, when I close or reload the browser tab, then the browser's own "Leave site?" prompt appears.
5. Given I haven't changed anything, or I've just saved, when I leave the form, then no warning appears.

# Jobs to Be Done

Why people use the Bill Splitting Calculator. Each job is something the person needs to get done whether or not this app exists, so no job mentions the app, its screens or its buttons. Each job names the role it belongs to (see [app-roles.md](app-roles.md)), and every story in [user-stories.md](user-stories.md) names the job it serves.

## Solo diner

**J1. Know exactly what I owe**
When I've finished a meal or a purchase on my own and the bill adds tax, extra fees and a tip, I want to know the exact amount to pay, to the cent, so I can pay the right amount without doing the maths in my head.
- Role: Solo diner

**J2. Keep a record of my own spending**
When I look back at what I've spent on meals and purchases, I want an accurate record of each past bill that I can correct or remove, so I can keep track of my spending and trust the numbers.
- Role: Solo diner

## Group member

**J3. Share a bill evenly**
When a group of us shares one bill and we agree to split it evenly, I want each person's share worked out so that the shares add up to exactly the bill, so I can make sure nobody pays a cent too much or too little.
- Role: Group member

**J4. Pay for what each person had**
When a group of us orders different things, including dishes some of us share, I want each person to pay for what they had plus a fair part of the tax, fees and tip, so I can make the split fair to people who ordered less.
- Role: Group member

**J5. Charge only the people who were there**
When one friend pays for an outing that only some of our friend group joined, I want to note who paid and who took part, so I can make sure only the people who were there owe a share and the person who paid gets it back.
- Role: Group member

**J6. Know who owes whom overall**
When my friends and I share costs again and again over weeks or months, I want to know at any moment what each person owes or is owed in total, and the fewest payments that would square everyone up, so I can settle debts without long lists of back-and-forth payments.
- Role: Group member

**J7. Count repayments**
When one friend pays another back, I want that repayment taken off what they owed, even if they pay back more than they owed, so I can keep everyone's running totals correct.
- Role: Group member

**J8. Include friends who don't keep records**
When some friends in our circle don't keep their own records of shared costs, I want to include them in our shared costs from the start and let them take over their own part whenever they choose to, so I can keep everyone's history complete.
- Role: Group member

**J9. See who changed what**
When anyone in our group adds, changes or removes a shared cost or a repayment, I want to see who did it, when, and what changed, so I can trust the totals and sort out disagreements.
- Role: Group member

**J10. Keep history right when people leave or come back**
When someone leaves our circle of friends, or comes back later, I want their past share to stay exactly as it was and their access to our shared records to end or return with them, so I can keep our history correct and keep it private to the people currently in the group.
- Role: Group member

**J11. Close out a group for good**
When I'm the last person still keeping a group's shared records and we're finished with them, I want to close them out completely, so I can leave nothing behind.
- Role: Group member

## Solo diner and Group member

**J12. Keep my money records private**
When I keep records of what I've spent, paid or am owed, I want only me, or only the friends a record concerns, to be able to see or change them, so I can trust that nobody else reads or alters my financial details.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J13. Get back in without help**
When I forget the secret I use to protect my records, I want a way to regain access that doesn't depend on anyone else, so I can make sure I never lose my history.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J14. Catch mistakes before relying on a figure**
When I'm working out money amounts and I make a typing mistake or enter something impossible, I want the mistake caught and clearly explained before I rely on the result, so I can never pay or charge someone the wrong amount.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J15. See amounts in my own currency**
When I pay in a particular currency, I want amounts shown with that currency's symbol and kept in one currency throughout, so I can read every figure without confusion.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J16. Use the browser I already have**
When I need to work out or check a bill, I want to do it in whichever common, up-to-date web browser I already use, so I can avoid installing or buying anything extra.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J20. See my overall position at a glance**
When I have money spent on my own and money owed between me and several groups of friends, I want one overview of what I owe and what I'm owed, so I can know where I stand without adding things up across places.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J21. Read figures comfortably in any light**
When I check money figures in a bright room or a dim restaurant at night, I want the display to suit the lighting and my own preference, so I can read amounts without strain.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J22. Manage money without a mouse or perfect eyesight**
When I rely on a keyboard, a screen reader, large text or high contrast, I want to do everything anyone else can do with my money records, so I can manage bills on my own without asking for help.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

## Host

**J17. Try it on my own computer for free**
When I want to try out or review a piece of software, I want to install and run my own copy on my computer with only free tools and no outside accounts or services, so I can evaluate it without paying or signing up for anything.
- Role: Host

**J18. Run it on my own server**
When I want my friends to use a tool for real, I want to run it on a server I control, without depending on any third-party company's services, so I can keep it running and keep our data with us.
- Role: Host

**J19. Get proof that it works**
When I evaluate a piece of software, I want quick, repeatable proof that it behaves as described in the common web browsers, so I can trust its claims without checking everything by hand.
- Role: Host

The frontend design is settled at 18.4% ambiguity, under the 20% target, and it's written into the spec (now v2.6) and the docs.

**Your frontend decisions:**

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Devices | **Desktop-first**, still fully usable on phones down to 360 px wide |
| Navigation | **Dashboard** after login, with your money totals per currency, your groups, recent solo bills and "New bill" buttons. A **left sidebar** becomes a menu button on phones. |
| Itemized bills | Each item has a **dropdown to pick one or more people** (your idea) |
| Results | Shown **below the form**, and the page scrolls to them |
| Group page | **Balances first**, with one-click "Record this payment", then tabs for Bills, Settle-ups, Members and Activity |
| Style | **Clean and calm**: white space, one accent color, red for "owes" and green for "is owed", always with +/− and words too |
| Dark mode | **Follows your device**, plus a Light/Dark/Device switch saved to your account |
| Accessibility | **WCAG 2.2 AA** (my reading of "best practice"), with automated checks in the tests |
| Feedback | Corner success messages, "Saving…" buttons that block double saves, loading placeholders, helpful empty screens, red confirm dialogs |
| Numbers | English text; amounts shown as **1,000,000.00** with the symbol first; typing "1,000.50" with a comma is accepted |
| Unsaved work | A **warning before leaving** a bill you haven't saved; no drafts |

**Docs updated:**
- **[jobs-to-be-done.md](docs/jobs-to-be-done.md):** 3 new jobs (J20–J22): seeing your overall position, reading comfortably in any light, and managing money without a mouse or perfect eyesight.
- **[user-stories.md](docs/user-stories.md):** 6 new stories (US-33 to US-38, all Not implemented), and new criteria in US-14, US-16, US-25 and US-26. The shared rules now include number display and layout.
- **[app-roles.md](docs/app-roles.md):** a note that both roles get the same screens and comforts.

**Checks:** all 38 stories are numbered correctly, every job has a story, no job mentions the app, and every frontend criterion in the spec appears in the docs.

**Choices I made that you didn't specify:**
- **Dashboard totals are per currency**, because groups can use different currencies and adding them together would give a wrong number.
- **The Account page holds only** your username, the appearance setting and Log out.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<tools-used-before-summary>AskUserQuestion, Bash, Edit, Read, SendUserFile, ToolSearch, Write, mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan, mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up, mcp__plugin_oh-my-claudecode_t__state_read, mcp__plugin_oh-my-claudecode_t__state_write</tools-used-before-summary>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Initial setup (done):** in the project folder `/Users/sanaarshad/Desktop/Sana-Arshad-calculator`, the user asked for:
     - a `src/` folder
     - a `docs/` folder with `app-roles.md`, `jobs-to-be-done.md` and `user-stories.md`, each holding just a title
     - an empty `transcripts/` folder
     - a `README.md` with empty headings
     - a proper `.gitignore`
     - git initialised, a first commit, and the folder structure shown
   - **Docs format rules:** the user gave rules for the three docs files and asked me to remember them. They're saved in memory and summarised in section 2.
   - **Requirements interview:** a deep interview (`--deep`) about the bill splitter. It produced the spec `.omc/specs/deep-interview-bill-splitter.md`. The user asked only to see the spec, not to build anything.
   - **Spec changes the user asked for, in order:**
     - an optional "Other charges" field
     - settling the open assumptions: the payer must be a participant; a settle-up can be any amount; removed-member rules; the invite code is view-and-copy only with no regeneration
     - the last member with an account can leave, with a warning, which permanently deletes the group
     - the invite code restores removed members
     - quick-split and 2-decimal % assumptions confirmed
   - **Docs:** fill the three docs files from the spec meticulously. Then a `--quick` gap interview settled 8 open questions plus 3 rules I had worked out myself.
   - **Name reuse:** member names can never be reused within a group.
   - **Commits:** commit the docs, and later merge to main.
   - **Git workflow:** the user said to commit straight to main, with no branches, PRs or merges.
   - **Database:** replace SQLite with a self-hosted Postgres container in the spec and docs.
   - **Frontend:** a deep interview on frontend design, then the spec and docs updated, then committed.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Stack:**
     - TypeScript throughout; React + Vite frontend
     - Node.js LTS + Express backend serving the API and the built frontend from one process
     - **Self-hosted PostgreSQL 18** in Docker Compose:
       - named volume; port bound to 127.0.0.1 only
       - `pg` (node-postgres) library; `DATABASE_URL` setting
       - migrations run automatically on server start; every save is one transaction
       - separate `bill_splitter_test` database, wiped and rebuilt on each test run
       - money stored as BIGINT whole cents; sessions stored in a Postgres table
     - **Tests:** Vitest; Playwright on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; axe accessibility checks
     - **Auth:** passwords hashed with `crypto.scrypt`; httpOnly SameSite session cookie
   - **Prerequisites and README steps:**
     - Node.js LTS + Docker
     - copy `.env.example` to `.env`, then `docker compose up -d`, `npm install`, `npm run dev`; tests with `npm test`
   - **Money math:**
     - whole cents only; % results rounded half-up
     - grand total = food + tax + other charges + tip
     - tax % and other charges % are of the food only; a % tip is on "food only" (default) or "food + tax", never on other charges
     - equal split: leftover cents go to the first participants in list order
     - itemized split: shared items split evenly; tax, other charges and tip each split in proportion to food, by largest remainder, ties to list order
   - **Groups:**
     - one payer per bill, who must be a participant
     - running balances that sum to 0; fewest suggested payments (greedy)
     - settle-ups can be any amount; overpaying flips the debt
   - **Accounts:**
     - username 3–30 characters (letters, numbers, _), not case-sensitive; password 8–128 characters
     - one-time recovery code; no limit on login attempts
     - Log out button; session ends after 30 days without use
   - **Limits:**
     - each money field 0.01–1,000,000.00 (the limit is per field; totals can be larger)
     - up to 200 items per bill; at least 1 item on every bill
     - group of 1–50 current members
     - tax and tip % 0–100 with 2 decimals
     - other charges optional: amount 0.01–1M, or % 0.01–100
   - **Names:**
     - group name 1–50 characters, required
     - member name 1–30 characters, required, never reused within a group (not case-sensitive), message "That name has already been used in this group"
     - bill name up to 60 characters, optional, default "Bill – date"
     - item name up to 40 characters, optional, default "Item N"
   - **Currency:** 12 symbols ($, €, £, ¥, ₹, Rs, ₩, ₺, R$, CHF, AED, SAR) plus "Other" (custom 1–3 characters, no digits). Each group's currency is fixed at creation. A solo bill's currency locks on first save.
   - **Frontend (v2.6):**
     - **Layout:** desktop-first, usable down to 360 px; Dashboard first (owe/owed per currency); left sidebar that becomes a menu on phones
     - **Bill screens:** a multi-select people dropdown on each item; results below the form, with a scroll to them after Calculate
     - **Group page:** balances first, with "Record this payment" pre-fill; tabs Bills, Settle-ups, Members, Activity
     - **Look:** clean and calm; dark mode follows the device, plus a Device/Light/Dark switch saved to the account
     - **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA, plus 24 px minimum touch targets
     - **Numbers:** English text; "1,000,000.00" display; symbol before the amount, with a space for letter symbols; typing accepts commas, rejects European style
     - **Feedback:** corner success messages for 5 s; "Saving…" buttons that block double saves; loading placeholders; empty-state screens; red confirm dialogs; unsaved-changes warning
   - **Removed members:**
     - removal only when the balance is 0.00
     - kept on old bills as "Name (removed)"; their bills are view-only until they're restored
     - lose access to the group
     - any member can restore them; entering the invite code auto-restores them
     - members can leave at 0.00
     - when the last member with an account leaves, a warning shows, then the group is permanently deleted
     - the activity log records everything
   - **User rules to follow, verbatim:**
     - Docs: "App Roles … 'A [role] is [who this person is and their situation]. They can [what they see and do in the app]. They must never [what the app must prevent]'" / "Jobs To Be Done … 'When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [expected outcome].' Each job names the role it belongs to … does not mention your app or its features" / "User Stories … 'As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit].' Each story names the job it serves and has acceptance criteria and a status … Given/When/Then … Cover the normal case and … invalid input, boundary values, very large or very small numbers, and what happens when the user carries on after a result or an error … Mark each story Implemented or Not implemented, based on what the app does today."
     - "Every user story i mark as Implemented works in the running app exactly as its acceptance criteria describe. Invalid input and error cases, such as division by zero, produce a clear message, never a crash or a wrong result."
     - No cloud: "no third-party services are attached to this app, or this app shouldn't be dependent on any cloud services or third-party paid services … does not mean that we cannot deploy this app on a server."
     - Git: "You do not need to create a new branch for every new commit or feature … I can manage the code history using commits only in a single branch."
     - Interview questions should be non-technical and show the cause and effect of each choice.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **`README.md`:** headings only: "# Bill Splitting Calculator", "## What It Is", "## Who It's For", "## Prerequisites", "## Installation", "## Running the App".
   - **`.gitignore`:**
     - ignores dependencies, build output, caches, coverage, logs, local DB files (*.sqlite, *.db …) and secrets (`.env`, `.env.*` but `!.env.example`, *.pem, *.key …)
     - also editor folders, OS files, `.claude/` and `.omc/`
     - `env/` and `vendor/` are anchored to the root
   - **`src/.gitkeep`, `transcripts/.gitkeep`:** placeholders so the empty folders are kept in git.
   - **`docs/app-roles.md`:**
     - 3 roles: Solo diner, Group member, Host, each with "can" and "must never" lists, plus a table of how the roles differ
     - notes: one account can hold both app roles; name-only members aren't a role; both app roles get the same screens and comforts
     - the Host role mentions Node.js LTS + Docker, `DATABASE_URL`, the separate test database, and never losing data on restart
   - **`docs/jobs-to-be-done.md`:**
     - jobs by role: Solo diner J1–J2; Group member J3–J11; both J12–J16 and J20–J22; Host J17–J19
     - none mention the app; J22 says "software that reads text aloud" rather than "screen reader"
   - **`docs/user-stories.md`:**
     - "How to read" and "Shared rules" sections (limits, names, currency, accounts, number display, layout)
     - a story table with 38 stories: US-01 to US-32 plus US-33 to US-38 for the frontend (Dashboard, navigation, light/dark, accessibility, feedback, unsaved changes)
     - every story is "Not implemented"
     - "Open questions: None"
   - **`.omc/specs/deep-interview-bill-splitter.md`** (gitignored, deliberately kept out of git; currently v2.6):
     - sections: Constraints (accounts, limits, names, currency, storage/Postgres), Non-Goals, Calculation Rules 1–12, Frontend Design (v2.6)
     - acceptance criteria groups: AC-F, AC-A, AC-S, AC-E, AC-I, AC-G, validation, AC-H, AC-T, AC-D
     - also: Roles, Assumptions table, Technical Context, Ontology, Open Assumptions (none), Transcript including change notes v2.1 to v2.6
   - **Memory files** (`/Users/sanaarshad/.claude/projects/-Users-sanaarshad-Desktop-Sana-Arshad-calculator/memory/`):
     - `MEMORY.md` (index)
     - `product-docs-requirements.md`
     - `no-third-party-services-rule.md`
     - `single-branch-git-workflow.md`
   - **Git history on `main` (the only branch):**
     - `773b5eb` Initial project structure
     - `50c198b` Add product docs
     - `b08f932` Update docs for self-hosted PostgreSQL
     - `8d4afea` Add frontend design to product docs
     - commits end with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
     - git identity set for this repo only: Sana Arshad / sanaarshad342@gmail.com
     - no remote and nothing pushed

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Plugin state in the first commit:** the `.omc/` folder was committed by accident. Fixed by adding `.omc/` to `.gitignore`, `git rm --cached`, and amending the commit.
   - **State tool overwrites:** `state_write` replaces the whole state rather than merging, so the full state is written every time.
   - **Branching:** I created the `docs/product-docs` branch. The user said not to branch, so I merged it (fast-forward), deleted it, and saved the single-branch rule to memory.
   - **Criteria numbering:** a US-31 criterion was out of order after an edit and was renumbered. Cross-check scripts verify numbering, job coverage, and that every quoted message and number from the spec appears in the docs.
   - **Details added without being asked:**
     - A "password change on Account page" and accepting a "%" sign when typing percentages were added to the frontend section without being asked; I removed both.
     - Other rules I added myself were flagged to the user and confirmed. One was rejected: reusing a removed member's name. Now names are never reused.
     - The user rejected the rule "the invite code can't bring back removed members"; the code now restores them.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Contradictions resolved:**
     - group size changed from 2–50 to 1–50 current members, because a group starts with only its creator
     - the dashboard shows totals per currency, never combined across currencies
     - the restore "same name" check was removed, since names are never reused
   - **Arithmetic checked with scripts:** for example the 26.00 / 134.00 / 54.00 / 13.50 examples, and the largest possible total of 1,000,000,000.00 (200 items × 1M, with 100% tax, 100% other charges and a 100% tip on food + tax).

   - Interview answers, including:

# Jobs to Be Done

Why people use the Bill Splitting Calculator. Each job is something the person needs to get done whether or not this app exists, so no job mentions the app, its screens or its buttons. Each job names the role it belongs to (see [app-roles.md](app-roles.md)), and every story in [user-stories.md](user-stories.md) names the job it serves.

## Solo diner

**J1. Know exactly what I owe**
When I've finished a meal or a purchase on my own and the bill adds tax, extra fees and a tip, I want to know the exact amount to pay, to the cent, so I can pay the right amount without doing the maths in my head.
- Role: Solo diner

**J2. Keep a record of my own spending**
When I look back at what I've spent on meals and purchases, I want an accurate record of each past bill that I can correct or remove, so I can keep track of my spending and trust the numbers.
- Role: Solo diner

## Group member

**J3. Share a bill evenly**
When a group of us shares one bill and we agree to split it evenly, I want each person's share worked out so that the shares add up to exactly the bill, so I can make sure nobody pays a cent too much or too little.
- Role: Group member

**J4. Pay for what each person had**
When a group of us orders different things, including dishes some of us share, I want each person to pay for what they had plus a fair part of the tax, fees and tip, so I can make the split fair to people who ordered less.
- Role: Group member

**J5. Charge only the people who were there**
When one friend pays for an outing that only some of our friend group joined, I want to note who paid and who took part, so I can make sure only the people who were there owe a share and the person who paid gets it back.
- Role: Group member

**J6. Know who owes whom overall**
When my friends and I share costs again and again over weeks or months, I want to know at any moment what each person owes or is owed in total, and the fewest payments that would square everyone up, so I can settle debts without long lists of back-and-forth payments.
- Role: Group member

**J7. Count repayments**
When one friend pays another back, I want that repayment taken off what they owed, even if they pay back more than they owed, so I can keep everyone's running totals correct.
- Role: Group member

**J8. Include friends who don't keep records**
When some friends in our circle don't keep their own records of shared costs, I want to include them in our shared costs from the start and let them take over their own part whenever they choose to, so I can keep everyone's history complete.
- Role: Group member

**J9. See who changed what**
When anyone in our group adds, changes or removes a shared cost or a repayment, I want to see who did it, when, and what changed, so I can trust the totals and sort out disagreements.
- Role: Group member

**J10. Keep history right when people leave or come back**
When someone leaves our circle of friends, or comes back later, I want their past share to stay exactly as it was and their access to our shared records to end or return with them, so I can keep our history correct and keep it private to the people currently in the group.
- Role: Group member

**J11. Close out a group for good**
When I'm the last person still keeping a group's shared records and we're finished with them, I want to close them out completely, so I can leave nothing behind.
- Role: Group member

## Solo diner and Group member

**J12. Keep my money records private**
When I keep records of what I've spent, paid or am owed, I want only me, or only the friends a record concerns, to be able to see or change them, so I can trust that nobody else reads or alters my financial details.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J13. Get back in without help**
When I forget the secret I use to protect my records, I want a way to regain access that doesn't depend on anyone else, so I can make sure I never lose my history.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J14. Catch mistakes before relying on a figure**
When I'm working out money amounts and I make a typing mistake or enter something impossible, I want the mistake caught and clearly explained before I rely on the result, so I can never pay or charge someone the wrong amount.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J15. See amounts in my own currency**
When I pay in a particular currency, I want amounts shown with that currency's symbol and kept in one currency throughout, so I can read every figure without confusion.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J16. Use the browser I already have**
When I need to work out or check a bill, I want to do it in whichever common, up-to-date web browser I already use, so I can avoid installing or buying anything extra.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J20. See my overall position at a glance**
When I have money spent on my own and money owed between me and several groups of friends, I want one overview of what I owe and what I'm owed, so I can know where I stand without adding things up across places.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J21. Read figures comfortably in any light**
When I check money figures in a bright room or a dim restaurant at night, I want the display to suit the lighting and my own preference, so I can read amounts without strain.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J22. Manage money without a mouse or perfect eyesight**
When I rely on a keyboard, software that reads text aloud, large text or high contrast, I want to do everything anyone else can do with my money records, so I can manage bills on my own without asking for help.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

## Host

**J17. Try it on my own computer for free**
When I want to try out or review a piece of software, I want to install and run my own copy on my computer with only free tools and no outside accounts or services, so I can evaluate it without paying or signing up for anything.
- Role: Host

**J18. Run it on my own server**
When I want my friends to use a tool for real, I want to run it on a server I control, without depending on any third-party company's services, so I can keep it running and keep our data with us.
- Role: Host

**J19. Get proof that it works**
When I evaluate a piece of software, I want quick, repeatable proof that it behaves as described in the common web browsers, so I can trust its claims without checking everything by hand.
- Role: Host
