1	# User Stories
2	
3	How the Bill Splitting Calculator helps each role get their jobs done. Every story names its role (from [app-roles.md](app-roles.md)) and the job it serves (from [jobs-to-be-done.md](jobs-to-be-done.md)), and has testable acceptance criteria and a status.
4	
5	## How to read this file
6	
7	- **Template:** "As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit]."
8	- **Acceptance criteria:** written as "Given [starting state], when [action], then [observable result]". They cover:
9	  - the normal case
10	  - invalid input
11	  - boundary values
12	  - very large and very small numbers
13	  - what happens when the user carries on after a result or an error
14	- **Status:** **Implemented** means the running app does exactly what every criterion says today. **Not implemented** means it doesn't yet. No app code exists yet, so every story is currently **Not implemented**.
15	- **Money format:** amounts are shown with 2 decimals and the bill's or group's currency symbol. The examples below leave out the symbol.
16	
17	## Shared rules used by many stories
18	
19	These rules come from the spec and apply wherever a story mentions them.
20	
21	- **Money fields** (item prices, settle-up amounts): 0.01–1,000,000.00, at most 2 decimal places. No negatives, letters, blanks or extra decimals.
22	- **Per-field limit:** the 1,000,000.00 limit applies to each field on its own. A bill's food subtotal and grand total may be larger.
23	- **Items:** every bill (solo, equal or itemized) needs 1–200 items. The largest possible grand total is 1,000,000,000.00, and it is still exact to the cent.
24	- **Names** (spaces at the start and end are trimmed before checking):
25	  - Group name: required, 1–50 characters.
26	  - Member name: required, 1–30 characters, and never reused within a group: it can't match any member the group has ever had, current or removed. Not case-sensitive: "omar" clashes with "Omar".
27	  - Bill name: optional, up to 60 characters, defaulting to "Bill – date".
28	  - Item name: optional, up to 40 characters, defaulting to "Item 1", "Item 2" and so on.
29	- **Tax and tip:** each can be a **%** (0–100, at most 2 decimal places, e.g. 12.5 or 8.25) or an **amount** (0.00–1,000,000.00). Tip may be 0.
30	- **Other charges** (optional, one field per bill, always labelled "Other charges", for service, delivery or table fees and similar):
31	  - Blank, 0 or 0.00 means "no other charges", and the results show "Other charges 0.00".
32	  - As an amount: 0.01–1,000,000.00, at most 2 decimal places.
33	  - As a %: 0.01–100, at most 2 decimal places.
34	- **What each % is of:**
35	  - Tax % and other charges % are always of the **food subtotal** only.
36	  - Tax is never charged on other charges or tip.
37	  - A % tip has a per-bill **"tip on"** option: **food only (default)** or **food + tax**. A tip is never calculated on other charges.
38	- **Rounding:** tax, other charges and tip are each worked out separately in cents. Any % result is rounded half-up to the cent, so it can be 0.00. A "food + tax" tip uses the already-rounded tax. All money math uses whole cents, never floating-point.
39	- **Grand total** = food subtotal + tax + other charges + tip.
40	- **Exactness:** for every bill, the shares add up exactly to the grand total.
41	- **Results:** totals appear only when **Calculate** is pressed. Changing any input hides the old result until Calculate is pressed again.
42	- **Currency:** a display symbol only, with no conversion. Choose from the default list of 12 ($, €, £, ¥, ₹, Rs, ₩, ₺, R$, CHF, AED, SAR), or choose "Other" and type a symbol of 1–3 characters with no digits.
43	- **Accounts:**
44	  - Username: 3–30 characters (letters, numbers, underscore), not case-sensitive.
45	  - Password: 8–128 characters, any characters.
46	  - A session ends on Log out or after 30 days without use.
47	  - There is no limit on failed login or recovery-code attempts.
48	- **Group size:** 1–50 **current** members. Removed members don't count.
49	- **Language and number display:**
50	  - All text is in English.
51	  - Amounts are shown with a thousands comma and 2 decimals ("1,000,000.00").
52	  - The currency symbol goes before the amount ("$12.50"), with a space for symbols made of letters ("Rs 400.00", "CHF 12.00").
53	  - Typing "1,000.50" is accepted as 1000.50, while European style ("1.000,50") is rejected.
54	- **Layout:** desktop-first, and fully usable on phones down to 360 px wide.
55	
56	## Story list
57	
58	| ID | Story | Role | Job | Status |
59	|---|---|---|---|---|
60	| US-01 | Create an account | Solo diner, Group member | J12 | Not implemented |
61	| US-02 | Log in and log out | Solo diner, Group member | J12 | Not implemented |
62	| US-03 | Reset a forgotten password with a recovery code | Solo diner, Group member | J13 | Not implemented |
63	| US-04 | Keep my bills and groups private | Solo diner, Group member | J12 | Not implemented |
64	| US-05 | Total a solo bill | Solo diner | J1 | Not implemented |
65	| US-06 | Choose the currency of a solo bill | Solo diner | J15 | Not implemented |
66	| US-07 | Save a solo bill to my history | Solo diner | J2 | Not implemented |
67	| US-08 | Open, edit and delete saved solo bills | Solo diner | J2 | Not implemented |
68	| US-09 | Create a group | Group member | J6 | Not implemented |
69	| US-10 | Add friends to a group by name | Group member | J8 | Not implemented |
70	| US-11 | View and copy the group's invite code | Group member | J8 | Not implemented |
71	| US-12 | Join a group by claiming my name | Group member | J8 | Not implemented |
72	| US-13 | Record an equal-split group bill | Group member | J3 | Not implemented |
73	| US-14 | Record an itemized group bill | Group member | J4 | Not implemented |
74	| US-15 | Record who paid a group bill | Group member | J5 | Not implemented |
75	| US-16 | See balances and suggested payments | Group member | J6 | Not implemented |
76	| US-17 | Record a settle-up | Group member | J7 | Not implemented |
77	| US-18 | Edit and delete group bills and settle-ups | Group member | J6 | Not implemented |
78	| US-19 | See the group's activity log | Group member | J9 | Not implemented |
79	| US-20 | Remove a member from a group | Group member | J10 | Not implemented |
80	| US-21 | Leave a group | Group member | J10 | Not implemented |
81	| US-22 | Close out a group as the last member with an account | Group member | J11 | Not implemented |
82	| US-23 | Restore a removed member | Group member | J10 | Not implemented |
83	| US-24 | Rejoin a group with the invite code | Group member | J10 | Not implemented |
84	| US-25 | Get a clear message for every invalid input | Solo diner, Group member | J14 | Not implemented |
85	| US-26 | Carry on safely after a result or an error | Solo diner, Group member | J14 | Not implemented |
86	| US-27 | Keep my inputs when saving fails | Solo diner, Group member | J14 | Not implemented |
87	| US-28 | Keep my records after a restart | Solo diner, Group member | J2, J6 | Not implemented |
88	| US-29 | Use the app in my usual browser | Solo diner, Group member | J16 | Not implemented |
89	| US-33 | See my money at a glance on the Dashboard | Solo diner, Group member | J20 | Not implemented |
90	| US-34 | Find my way on a computer or a phone | Solo diner, Group member | J16 | Not implemented |
91	| US-35 | Choose light or dark appearance | Solo diner, Group member | J21 | Not implemented |
92	| US-36 | Use the app with a keyboard, screen reader or zoom | Solo diner, Group member | J22 | Not implemented |
93	| US-37 | Know what happened after every action | Solo diner, Group member | J14 | Not implemented |
94	| US-38 | Don't lose unsaved changes by accident | Solo diner, Group member | J14 | Not implemented |
95	| US-30 | Run the app locally from the README | Host | J17 | Not implemented |
96	| US-31 | Deploy the app to my own server | Host | J18 | Not implemented |
97	| US-32 | Run all tests with one command | Host | J19 | Not implemented |
98	
99	---
100	
101	## Accounts
102	
103	### US-01 Create an account
104	**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** to create an account with a username and password, **so that** my bills and groups are kept for me and nobody else.
105	- **Job:** J12 · **Status:** Not implemented
106	
107	Acceptance criteria:
108	1. Given a username nobody has used and a valid password, when I sign up, then my account is created, I'm logged in, and a one-time recovery code is shown with a "save this now" warning.
109	2. Given I leave the recovery code screen, then that code is never shown again.
110	3. Given a username that is already taken, when I sign up, then I see "That username is taken" and no account is created.
111	4. Given "Sana" already exists, when someone signs up as "sana" or "SANA", then they see "That username is taken" (usernames aren't case-sensitive).
112	5. Given a username that is blank, 2 characters or 31 characters long, or contains anything other than letters, numbers and underscore (e.g. "sana!" or "sa na"), when I sign up, then a clear message is shown and no account is created.
113	6. Given a username of exactly 3 or exactly 30 characters, then it's accepted.
114	7. Given a password that is blank, 7 characters or 129 characters long, when I sign up, then a clear message is shown and no account is created.
115	8. Given a password of exactly 8 or exactly 128 characters, including spaces and symbols, then it's accepted.
116	9. Given sign-up failed (e.g. the username was taken), when I fix it and sign up again, then the account is created without reloading the page.
117	10. The app never asks for an email address or phone number, and never sends email or text messages.
118	
119	### US-02 Log in and log out
120	**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** to log in with my username and password and log out when I'm done, **so that** only I can reach my records, even on a shared computer.
121	- **Job:** J12 · **Status:** Not implemented
122	
123	Acceptance criteria:
124	1. Given a correct username and password, when I log in, then I'm logged in and see my own bills and groups.
125	2. Given a wrong password, when I log in, then I see "Username or password is incorrect" and stay logged out.
126	3. Given a username that doesn't exist, when I log in, then I see the same message, "Username or password is incorrect", which never says whether the username or the password was wrong.
127	4. Given a failed login, when I enter the correct details and log in again, then I'm logged in without reloading the page.
128	5. Given my account is "Sana", when I log in as "sana" or "SANA" with the right password, then I'm logged in.
129	6. Given 20 wrong passwords in a row, when I then enter the correct one, then I'm logged in. There's no limit on attempts.
130	7. Given I'm logged in, when I press Log out, then I'm logged out at once, and opening any bill or group page sends me to the login page.
131	8. Given I've used the app within the last 30 days, when I return, then I'm still logged in.
132	9. Given I haven't used the app for 30 days, when I return, then I must log in again.
133	
134	### US-03 Reset a forgotten password with a recovery code
135	**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** to set a new password using my recovery code, **so that** I can get back into my account without email or anyone's help.
136	- **Job:** J13 · **Status:** Not implemented
137	
138	Acceptance criteria:
139	1. Given my username, my current recovery code and a new valid password, when I reset, then I can log in with the new password, and a new recovery code is shown once with a "save this now" warning.
140	2. Given I've reset my password, when I try the old recovery code again, then it no longer works.
141	3. Given a wrong recovery code, or a username that doesn't exist, when I reset, then a clear message is shown and no password is changed.
142	4. Given a new password that is blank, 7 characters or 129 characters long, when I reset, then a clear message is shown and the password isn't changed.
143	5. Given many wrong recovery codes in a row, when I then enter the right one, then the reset works. There's no limit on attempts.
144	6. Given I've lost both my password and my recovery code, then the account can't be recovered. My names in groups stay as they were, and a new account can claim a name again through the group's invite code (US-12, US-24).
145	
146	### US-04 Keep my bills and groups private
147	**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** my solo bills to be visible only to me and my groups only to their current members, **so that** nobody else can read or change my money records.
148	- **Job:** J12 · **Status:** Not implemented
149	
150	Acceptance criteria:
151	1. Given I'm logged out, when I open any bill or group page (including by typing its address), then I'm sent to the login page and no data is shown.
152	2. Given I'm logged in, when I type the address of another account's solo bill, then it isn't shown and can't be changed.
153	3. Given I'm logged in, when I type the address of a group I'm not a current member of (including one I was removed from), then it isn't shown and can't be changed.
154	4. Given someone sends requests straight to the server, bypassing the page, then the server applies the same rules and returns no private data.
155	
156	---
157	
158	## Solo bills
159	
160	### US-05 Total a solo bill
161	**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to enter my bill's items, tax, other charges and tip and see the exact total, **so that** I pay the right amount.
162	- **Job:** J1 · **Status:** Not implemented
163	
164	Acceptance criteria:
165	1. Given items 12.50 and 7.50, tax 10%, other charges blank and tip 15% on food, when I press Calculate, then I see subtotal 20.00, tax 2.00, other charges 0.00, tip 3.00 and total 25.00.
166	2. Given items 12.50 and 7.50, tax 10%, other charges 5% and tip 15% on food, when I press Calculate, then I see subtotal 20.00, tax 2.00, other charges 1.00, tip 3.00 and total 26.00.
167	3. Given food 100.00, tax 10.00 (amount), other charges blank and tip 15% on food + tax, when I press Calculate, then the tip is 16.50 and the total is 126.50.
168	4. Given food 100.00, tax 10.00 (amount), other charges 7.50 (amount) and tip 15% on food + tax, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 7.50, the tip is 16.50 (other charges are not tipped on), and the total is 134.00.
169	5. Given food 100.00, tax 10% and other charges 10%, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 10.00 (a % of the food only, not of food + tax).
170	6. Given food 33.33 and other charges 12.5%, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 4.17 (4.16625 rounded half-up).
171	7. Given food 20.00 and tip 12.5%, then the tip is 2.50. Given food 20.00 and tax 8.25%, then the tax is 1.65.
172	8. Given food 0.01 and other charges 5%, then other charges is 0.00 (rounded half-up) and no error is shown.
173	9. Given other charges 0 or 0.00, then it's treated as "no other charges", shows 0.00, and causes no error.
174	10. Given tip 0, then the tip shows 0.00 with no error.
175	11. Given a new bill, then the "tip on" option starts at food only.
176	12. Given food 0.01, tax 0, other charges 1,000,000.00 (amount) and tip 0, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 1,000,000.00 and the total is 1,000,000.01.
177	13. Given no items, when I press Calculate, then I see "Add at least one item" and no result.
178	14. Given any invalid field (see US-25), when I press Calculate, then no result is shown.
179	
180	### US-06 Choose the currency of a solo bill
181	**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to pick the currency symbol for my bill, **so that** amounts are shown the way I paid them.
182	- **Job:** J15 · **Status:** Not implemented
183	
184	Acceptance criteria:
185	1. Given a new solo bill, when I open the currency picker, then it offers exactly $, €, £, ¥, ₹, Rs, ₩, ₺, R$, CHF, AED, SAR and "Other".
186	2. Given I pick a symbol from the list, then every amount on the bill is shown with that symbol, and no currency conversion happens.
187	3. Given I pick "Other" and type "kr" or "zł", then every amount is shown with that symbol.
188	4. Given "Other" with a blank symbol, a symbol of 4+ characters (e.g. "abcd") or one containing a digit (e.g. "R1"), when I press Calculate or Save, then I see "Currency symbol must be 1–3 characters with no digits" and nothing is saved.
189	5. Given "Other" with " kr " (spaces around it), then it's saved as "kr".
190	6. Given an unsaved bill, I can change its currency freely.
191	7. Given the bill has been saved once, when I edit it, then the currency can't be changed.
192	8. Given an invalid currency symbol is sent straight to the server, then it's rejected and nothing is saved.
193	
194	### US-07 Save a solo bill to my history
195	**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to save a bill and see it in my history, **so that** I have a record of what I spent.
196	- **Job:** J2 · **Status:** Not implemented
197	
198	Acceptance criteria:
199	1. Given a valid solo bill, when I save it, then it appears at the top of my history (newest first) showing its name, date, currency and total.
200	2. Given I leave the name empty, when I save, then the bill is named "Bill – date" (using the bill's date).
201	3. Given a bill name of exactly 60 characters, then it's accepted. A name of 61 or more characters shows a clear message and the bill isn't saved.
202	4. Given the bill has an invalid field (see US-25), when I press Save, then the field's message is shown and nothing is saved.
203	5. Given I have several saved bills, then my history lists them newest first, and shows only my own bills.
204	
205	### US-08 Open, edit and delete saved solo bills
206	**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to reopen, fix or remove a saved bill, **so that** my record stays accurate.
207	- **Job:** J2 · **Status:** Not implemented
208	
209	Acceptance criteria:
210	1. Given a saved solo bill, when I open it, then every input and result is shown exactly as saved, including other charges and its % / amount setting, and the "tip on" setting.
211	2. Given I change an amount and save, then the totals are recalculated and checked with the same rules as a new bill. Invalid edits show the same messages and aren't saved.
212	3. Given I edit other charges (value or % / amount), when I save, then the total is recalculated to match.
213	4. Given I'm editing a saved bill, then its currency can't be changed.
214	5. Given I press Delete, then I'm asked to confirm. Cancel keeps the bill unchanged, and Confirm removes it from my history.
215	
216	---
217	
218	## Groups
219	
220	### US-09 Create a group
221	**As a** Group member, **I want** to create a group for a circle of friends, **so that** we can keep shared costs in one place over time.
222	- **Job:** J6 · **Status:** Not implemented
223	
224	Acceptance criteria:
225	1. Given I enter a group name and pick a currency, when I create the group, then I'm its first and only current member, an invite code is generated automatically, and the activity log records "X created the group".
226	2. Given I'm choosing the group's currency, then I can pick from the default list of 12 or choose "Other" and type a symbol of 1–3 characters with no digits (same rules and message as US-06). A note tells me the currency can't be changed after the group is created.
227	3. Given a blank group name, or one of 51 or more characters, when I create the group, then a clear message is shown and no group is created. Names of exactly 1 and exactly 50 characters are accepted.
228	4. Given a group exists, then there's no way to change its currency, either on the page or by sending requests straight to the server.
229	5. Given a group, then all its bills, settle-ups and balances use the group's single currency.
230	
231	### US-10 Add friends to a group by name
232	**As a** Group member, **I want** to add a friend to my group by name only, **so that** I can include them in bills even if they never create an account.
233	- **Job:** J8 · **Status:** Not implemented
234	
235	Acceptance criteria:
236	1. Given I add a name-only member "Omar", then Omar can immediately be ticked as a participant, and chosen as the payer of a bill he takes part in, and the activity log records "X added Omar".
237	2. Given the group has 50 current members, when I add another, then I see "A group can have at most 50 members" and nobody is added.
238	3. Given a blank name, or one of 31 or more characters, when I add it, then a clear message is shown and nobody is added. Names of exactly 1 and exactly 30 characters are accepted.
239	4. Given "Omar" is a current member, when I add "Omar", "omar" or "OMAR", then I see "That name has already been used in this group" and nobody is added.
240	5. Given "Omar" is a removed member, when I add a new "Omar" (in any letter case), then I see "That name has already been used in this group" and nobody is added. The name stays Omar's, so restoring him always gives it back.
241	6. Given 49 current members and some removed members, when I add one more, then it succeeds, because removed members don't count toward the 50.
242	
243	### US-11 View and copy the group's invite code
244	**As a** Group member, **I want** to see and copy my group's invite code, **so that** I can pass it to friends who want to take over their own name.
245	- **Job:** J8 · **Status:** Not implemented
246	
247	Acceptance criteria:
248	1. Given I'm a current member, when I open the group's invite section, then I see the invite code and a Copy button.
249	2. Given I press Copy, then the code is copied, ready to paste.
250	3. Given any group, then there's no option to regenerate or change the invite code. It stays the same for the life of the group.
251	
252	### US-12 Join a group by claiming my name
253	**As a** Group member, **I want** to enter a group's invite code and claim the name my friends added for me, **so that** I can see and manage my own part of the group's history.
254	- **Job:** J8 · **Status:** Not implemented
255	
256	Acceptance criteria:
257	1. Given Omar creates an account and enters the group's invite code, when he chooses "I'm Omar", then his account is linked to that member, the group appears in his group list, he sees the full group history, and the activity log records "Omar claimed the name Omar".
258	2. Given a valid invite code and an account that isn't in the group, when I enter it, then I can choose from all of the group's **unclaimed** members, current or removed. Removed names are marked "(removed)".
259	3. Given a member already claimed by an account, then that name isn't offered, and no other account can claim it.
260	4. Given my account already claims a member in this group, then I can't claim a second member in the same group.
261	5. Given a valid invite code, then there's no option to add myself as a new name. Only current members add new names (US-10).
262	6. Given a new account claims a removed, unclaimed name, then that member is restored and linked to the account (restore limits from US-23 apply).
263	7. Given a wrong invite code, when I enter it, then I see "That invite code isn't valid" and join nothing.
264	8. Given I'm already a current member, when I enter the group's invite code, then I see "You're already in this group" and nothing changes.
265	9. Given a wrong code was entered, when I enter the correct code, then joining works without reloading the page.
266	
267	---
268	
269	## Group bills
270	
271	### US-13 Record an equal-split group bill
272	**As a** Group member, **I want** to record a group bill split evenly between the people who took part, **so that** each pays an equal share that adds up exactly to the bill.
273	- **Job:** J3 · **Status:** Not implemented

576	2. Given the README, then it never asks for a paid account, an API key, or any third-party cloud or paid service.
577	3. Given the app is running, then it works with no internet-based service: accounts, data storage and calculations all happen inside the app and its own self-hosted PostgreSQL container.
578	4. Given the database container isn't running, when I start the app, then it prints "Can't reach the database. Start it with: docker compose up -d" and stops, with no crash trace.
579	5. Given a fresh database, when the app starts, then it creates its own tables automatically. No manual database setup is needed.
580	6. Given the database container is running, then its port is reachable only from my own computer, not from other machines on the network.
581	7. Given the README, then it warns that `docker compose down -v` permanently deletes all saved data, and that plain `docker compose down` keeps it.
582	
583	### US-31 Deploy the app to my own server
584	**As a** Host, **I want** to run the same app on a server, **so that** my friends can use it for real.
585	- **Job:** J18 · **Status:** Not implemented
586	
587	Acceptance criteria:
588	1. Given a server with Node.js LTS and a self-hosted PostgreSQL 18 database (e.g. the same Compose file), when I deploy the same build, then it runs, configured only through settings the app owns: port, `DATABASE_URL` and session secret.
589	2. Given the deployed app, then it doesn't depend on any third-party cloud or paid service.
590	3. Given the deployed app, then passwords are stored hashed (never as plain text), and sessions use secure cookies.
591	4. Given the deployed app starts against a database that already has data, then pending schema updates are applied automatically and existing data is kept.
592	
593	### US-32 Run all tests with one command
594	**As a** Host, **I want** to run every automated test with one command, **so that** I can see for myself that the app works as described.
595	- **Job:** J19 · **Status:** Not implemented
596	
597	Acceptance criteria:
598	1. Given the project is installed and the database container is running, when I run `npm test`, then the calculation, validation and server tests and the browser tests (Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, Safari's engine) all run and pass.
599	2. Given I have real bills saved in the app, when I run `npm test`, then the tests use only the separate test database, which is wiped and rebuilt at the start of each run, and my real data is unchanged.
600	3. Given I run `npm test` twice in a row, then both runs give the same results.
601	4. Given the database container isn't running, when I run `npm test`, then it stops at once with "Can't reach the database. Start it with: docker compose up -d".
602	
603	---
604	
605	## Open questions
606	
607	None. Every open question has been settled in the spec and is reflected in the stories above.
608

# User Stories

How the Bill Splitting Calculator helps each role get their jobs done. Every story names its role (from [app-roles.md](app-roles.md)) and the job it serves (from [jobs-to-be-done.md](jobs-to-be-done.md)), and has testable acceptance criteria and a status.

## How to read this file

- **Template:** "As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit]."
- **Acceptance criteria:** written as "Given [starting state], when [action], then [observable result]". They cover:
  - the normal case
  - invalid input
  - boundary values
  - very large and very small numbers
  - what happens when the user carries on after a result or an error
- **Status:** **Implemented** means the running app does exactly what every criterion says today. **Not implemented** means it doesn't yet. No app code exists yet, so every story is currently **Not implemented**.
- **Money format:** amounts are shown with 2 decimals and the bill's or group's currency symbol. The examples below leave out the symbol.

## Shared rules used by many stories

These rules come from the spec and apply wherever a story mentions them.

- **Money fields** (item prices, settle-up amounts): 0.01–1,000,000.00, at most 2 decimal places. No negatives, letters, blanks or extra decimals.
- **Per-field limit:** the 1,000,000.00 limit applies to each field on its own. A bill's food subtotal and grand total may be larger.
- **Items:** every bill (solo, equal or itemized) needs 1–200 items. The largest possible grand total is 1,000,000,000.00, and it is still exact to the cent.
- **Names** (spaces at the start and end are trimmed before checking):
  - Group name: required, 1–50 characters.
  - Member name: required, 1–30 characters, and never reused within a group: it can't match any member the group has ever had, current or removed. Not case-sensitive: "omar" clashes with "Omar".
  - Bill name: optional, up to 60 characters, defaulting to "Bill – date".
  - Item name: optional, up to 40 characters, defaulting to "Item 1", "Item 2" and so on.
- **Tax and tip:** each can be a **%** (0–100, at most 2 decimal places, e.g. 12.5 or 8.25) or an **amount** (0.00–1,000,000.00). Tip may be 0.
- **Other charges** (optional, one field per bill, always labelled "Other charges", for service, delivery or table fees and similar):
  - Blank, 0 or 0.00 means "no other charges", and the results show "Other charges 0.00".
  - As an amount: 0.01–1,000,000.00, at most 2 decimal places.
  - As a %: 0.01–100, at most 2 decimal places.
- **What each % is of:**
  - Tax % and other charges % are always of the **food subtotal** only.
  - Tax is never charged on other charges or tip.
  - A % tip has a per-bill **"tip on"** option: **food only (default)** or **food + tax**. A tip is never calculated on other charges.
- **Rounding:** tax, other charges and tip are each worked out separately in cents. Any % result is rounded half-up to the cent, so it can be 0.00. A "food + tax" tip uses the already-rounded tax. All money math uses whole cents, never floating-point.
- **Grand total** = food subtotal + tax + other charges + tip.
- **Exactness:** for every bill, the shares add up exactly to the grand total.
- **Results:** totals appear only when **Calculate** is pressed. Changing any input hides the old result until Calculate is pressed again.
- **Currency:** a display symbol only, with no conversion. Choose from the default list of 12 ($, €, £, ¥, ₹, Rs, ₩, ₺, R$, CHF, AED, SAR), or choose "Other" and type a symbol of 1–3 characters with no digits.
- **Accounts:**
  - Username: 3–30 characters (letters, numbers, underscore), not case-sensitive.
  - Password: 8–128 characters, any characters.
  - A session ends on Log out or after 30 days without use.
  - There is no limit on failed login or recovery-code attempts.
- **Group size:** 1–50 **current** members. Removed members don't count.
- **Language and number display:**
  - All text is in English.
  - Amounts are shown with a thousands comma and 2 decimals ("1,000,000.00").
  - The currency symbol goes before the amount ("$12.50"), with a space for symbols made of letters ("Rs 400.00", "CHF 12.00").
  - Typing "1,000.50" is accepted as 1000.50, while European style ("1.000,50") is rejected.
- **Layout:** desktop-first, and fully usable on phones down to 360 px wide.

## Story list

| ID | Story | Role | Job | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| US-01 | Create an account | Solo diner, Group member | J12 | Not implemented |
| US-02 | Log in and log out | Solo diner, Group member | J12 | Not implemented |
| US-03 | Reset a forgotten password with a recovery code | Solo diner, Group member | J13 | Not implemented |
| US-04 | Keep my bills and groups private | Solo diner, Group member | J12 | Not implemented |
| US-05 | Total a solo bill | Solo diner | J1 | Not implemented |
| US-06 | Choose the currency of a solo bill | Solo diner | J15 | Not implemented |
| US-07 | Save a solo bill to my history | Solo diner | J2 | Not implemented |
| US-08 | Open, edit and delete saved solo bills | Solo diner | J2 | Not implemented |
| US-09 | Create a group | Group member | J6 | Not implemented |
| US-10 | Add friends to a group by name | Group member | J8 | Not implemented |
| US-11 | View and copy the group's invite code | Group member | J8 | Not implemented |
| US-12 | Join a group by claiming my name | Group member | J8 | Not implemented |
| US-13 | Record an equal-split group bill | Group member | J3 | Not implemented |
| US-14 | Record an itemized group bill | Group member | J4 | Not implemented |
| US-15 | Record who paid a group bill | Group member | J5 | Not implemented |
| US-16 | See balances and suggested payments | Group member | J6 | Not implemented |
| US-17 | Record a settle-up | Group member | J7 | Not implemented |
| US-18 | Edit and delete group bills and settle-ups | Group member | J6 | Not implemented |
| US-19 | See the group's activity log | Group member | J9 | Not implemented |
| US-20 | Remove a member from a group | Group member | J10 | Not implemented |
| US-21 | Leave a group | Group member | J10 | Not implemented |
| US-22 | Close out a group as the last member with an account | Group member | J11 | Not implemented |
| US-23 | Restore a removed member | Group member | J10 | Not implemented |
| US-24 | Rejoin a group with the invite code | Group member | J10 | Not implemented |
| US-25 | Get a clear message for every invalid input | Solo diner, Group member | J14 | Not implemented |
| US-26 | Carry on safely after a result or an error | Solo diner, Group member | J14 | Not implemented |
| US-27 | Keep my inputs when saving fails | Solo diner, Group member | J14 | Not implemented |
| US-28 | Keep my records after a restart | Solo diner, Group member | J2, J6 | Not implemented |
| US-29 | Use the app in my usual browser | Solo diner, Group member | J16 | Not implemented |
| US-33 | See my money at a glance on the Dashboard | Solo diner, Group member | J20 | Not implemented |
| US-34 | Find my way on a computer or a phone | Solo diner, Group member | J16 | Not implemented |
| US-35 | Choose light or dark appearance | Solo diner, Group member | J21 | Not implemented |
| US-36 | Use the app with a keyboard, screen reader or zoom | Solo diner, Group member | J22 | Not implemented |
| US-37 | Know what happened after every action | Solo diner, Group member | J14 | Not implemented |
| US-38 | Don't lose unsaved changes by accident | Solo diner, Group member | J14 | Not implemented |
| US-30 | Run the app locally from the README | Host | J17 | Not implemented |
| US-31 | Deploy the app to my own server | Host | J18 | Not implemented |
| US-32 | Run all tests with one command | Host | J19 | Not implemented |

---

## Accounts

### US-01 Create an account
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** to create an account with a username and password, **so that** my bills and groups are kept for me and nobody else.
- **Job:** J12 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a username nobody has used and a valid password, when I sign up, then my account is created, I'm logged in, and a one-time recovery code is shown with a "save this now" warning.
2. Given I leave the recovery code screen, then that code is never shown again.
3. Given a username that is already taken, when I sign up, then I see "That username is taken" and no account is created.
4. Given "Sana" already exists, when someone signs up as "sana" or "SANA", then they see "That username is taken" (usernames aren't case-sensitive).
5. Given a username that is blank, 2 characters or 31 characters long, or contains anything other than letters, numbers and underscore (e.g. "sana!" or "sa na"), when I sign up, then a clear message is shown and no account is created.
6. Given a username of exactly 3 or exactly 30 characters, then it's accepted.
7. Given a password that is blank, 7 characters or 129 characters long, when I sign up, then a clear message is shown and no account is created.
8. Given a password of exactly 8 or exactly 128 characters, including spaces and symbols, then it's accepted.
9. Given sign-up failed (e.g. the username was taken), when I fix it and sign up again, then the account is created without reloading the page.
10. The app never asks for an email address or phone number, and never sends email or text messages.

### US-02 Log in and log out
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** to log in with my username and password and log out when I'm done, **so that** only I can reach my records, even on a shared computer.
- **Job:** J12 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a correct username and password, when I log in, then I'm logged in and see my own bills and groups.
2. Given a wrong password, when I log in, then I see "Username or password is incorrect" and stay logged out.
3. Given a username that doesn't exist, when I log in, then I see the same message, "Username or password is incorrect", which never says whether the username or the password was wrong.
4. Given a failed login, when I enter the correct details and log in again, then I'm logged in without reloading the page.
5. Given my account is "Sana", when I log in as "sana" or "SANA" with the right password, then I'm logged in.
6. Given 20 wrong passwords in a row, when I then enter the correct one, then I'm logged in. There's no limit on attempts.
7. Given I'm logged in, when I press Log out, then I'm logged out at once, and opening any bill or group page sends me to the login page.
8. Given I've used the app within the last 30 days, when I return, then I'm still logged in.
9. Given I haven't used the app for 30 days, when I return, then I must log in again.

### US-03 Reset a forgotten password with a recovery code
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** to set a new password using my recovery code, **so that** I can get back into my account without email or anyone's help.
- **Job:** J13 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given my username, my current recovery code and a new valid password, when I reset, then I can log in with the new password, and a new recovery code is shown once with a "save this now" warning.
2. Given I've reset my password, when I try the old recovery code again, then it no longer works.
3. Given a wrong recovery code, or a username that doesn't exist, when I reset, then a clear message is shown and no password is changed.
4. Given a new password that is blank, 7 characters or 129 characters long, when I reset, then a clear message is shown and the password isn't changed.
5. Given many wrong recovery codes in a row, when I then enter the right one, then the reset works. There's no limit on attempts.
6. Given I've lost both my password and my recovery code, then the account can't be recovered. My names in groups stay as they were, and a new account can claim a name again through the group's invite code (US-12, US-24).

### US-04 Keep my bills and groups private
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** my solo bills to be visible only to me and my groups only to their current members, **so that** nobody else can read or change my money records.
- **Job:** J12 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I'm logged out, when I open any bill or group page (including by typing its address), then I'm sent to the login page and no data is shown.
2. Given I'm logged in, when I type the address of another account's solo bill, then it isn't shown and can't be changed.
3. Given I'm logged in, when I type the address of a group I'm not a current member of (including one I was removed from), then it isn't shown and can't be changed.
4. Given someone sends requests straight to the server, bypassing the page, then the server applies the same rules and returns no private data.

---

## Solo bills

### US-05 Total a solo bill
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to enter my bill's items, tax, other charges and tip and see the exact total, **so that** I pay the right amount.
- **Job:** J1 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given items 12.50 and 7.50, tax 10%, other charges blank and tip 15% on food, when I press Calculate, then I see subtotal 20.00, tax 2.00, other charges 0.00, tip 3.00 and total 25.00.
2. Given items 12.50 and 7.50, tax 10%, other charges 5% and tip 15% on food, when I press Calculate, then I see subtotal 20.00, tax 2.00, other charges 1.00, tip 3.00 and total 26.00.
3. Given food 100.00, tax 10.00 (amount), other charges blank and tip 15% on food + tax, when I press Calculate, then the tip is 16.50 and the total is 126.50.
4. Given food 100.00, tax 10.00 (amount), other charges 7.50 (amount) and tip 15% on food + tax, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 7.50, the tip is 16.50 (other charges are not tipped on), and the total is 134.00.
5. Given food 100.00, tax 10% and other charges 10%, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 10.00 (a % of the food only, not of food + tax).
6. Given food 33.33 and other charges 12.5%, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 4.17 (4.16625 rounded half-up).
7. Given food 20.00 and tip 12.5%, then the tip is 2.50. Given food 20.00 and tax 8.25%, then the tax is 1.65.
8. Given food 0.01 and other charges 5%, then other charges is 0.00 (rounded half-up) and no error is shown.
9. Given other charges 0 or 0.00, then it's treated as "no other charges", shows 0.00, and causes no error.
10. Given tip 0, then the tip shows 0.00 with no error.
11. Given a new bill, then the "tip on" option starts at food only.
12. Given food 0.01, tax 0, other charges 1,000,000.00 (amount) and tip 0, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 1,000,000.00 and the total is 1,000,000.01.
13. Given no items, when I press Calculate, then I see "Add at least one item" and no result.
14. Given any invalid field (see US-25), when I press Calculate, then no result is shown.

### US-06 Choose the currency of a solo bill
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to pick the currency symbol for my bill, **so that** amounts are shown the way I paid them.
- **Job:** J15 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a new solo bill, when I open the currency picker, then it offers exactly $, €, £, ¥, ₹, Rs, ₩, ₺, R$, CHF, AED, SAR and "Other".
2. Given I pick a symbol from the list, then every amount on the bill is shown with that symbol, and no currency conversion happens.
3. Given I pick "Other" and type "kr" or "zł", then every amount is shown with that symbol.
4. Given "Other" with a blank symbol, a symbol of 4+ characters (e.g. "abcd") or one containing a digit (e.g. "R1"), when I press Calculate or Save, then I see "Currency symbol must be 1–3 characters with no digits" and nothing is saved.
5. Given "Other" with " kr " (spaces around it), then it's saved as "kr".
6. Given an unsaved bill, I can change its currency freely.
7. Given the bill has been saved once, when I edit it, then the currency can't be changed.
8. Given an invalid currency symbol is sent straight to the server, then it's rejected and nothing is saved.

### US-07 Save a solo bill to my history
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to save a bill and see it in my history, **so that** I have a record of what I spent.
- **Job:** J2 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a valid solo bill, when I save it, then it appears at the top of my history (newest first) showing its name, date, currency and total.
2. Given I leave the name empty, when I save, then the bill is named "Bill – date" (using the bill's date).
3. Given a bill name of exactly 60 characters, then it's accepted. A name of 61 or more characters shows a clear message and the bill isn't saved.
4. Given the bill has an invalid field (see US-25), when I press Save, then the field's message is shown and nothing is saved.
5. Given I have several saved bills, then my history lists them newest first, and shows only my own bills.

### US-08 Open, edit and delete saved solo bills
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to reopen, fix or remove a saved bill, **so that** my record stays accurate.
- **Job:** J2 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a saved solo bill, when I open it, then every input and result is shown exactly as saved, including other charges and its % / amount setting, and the "tip on" setting.
2. Given I change an amount and save, then the totals are recalculated and checked with the same rules as a new bill. Invalid edits show the same messages and aren't saved.
3. Given I edit other charges (value or % / amount), when I save, then the total is recalculated to match.
4. Given I'm editing a saved bill, then its currency can't be changed.
5. Given I press Delete, then I'm asked to confirm. Cancel keeps the bill unchanged, and Confirm removes it from my history.

---

## Groups

### US-09 Create a group
**As a** Group member, **I want** to create a group for a circle of friends, **so that** we can keep shared costs in one place over time.
- **Job:** J6 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I enter a group name and pick a currency, when I create the group, then I'm its first and only current member, an invite code is generated automatically, and the activity log records "X created the group".
2. Given I'm choosing the group's currency, then I can pick from the default list of 12 or choose "Other" and type a symbol of 1–3 characters with no digits (same rules and message as US-06). A note tells me the currency can't be changed after the group is created.
3. Given a blank group name, or one of 51 or more characters, when I create the group, then a clear message is shown and no group is created. Names of exactly 1 and exactly 50 characters are accepted.
4. Given a group exists, then there's no way to change its currency, either on the page or by sending requests straight to the server.
5. Given a group, then all its bills, settle-ups and balances use the group's single currency.

### US-10 Add friends to a group by name
**As a** Group member, **I want** to add a friend to my group by name only, **so that** I can include them in bills even if they never create an account.
- **Job:** J8 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I add a name-only member "Omar", then Omar can immediately be ticked as a participant, and chosen as the payer of a bill he takes part in, and the activity log records "X added Omar".
2. Given the group has 50 current members, when I add another, then I see "A group can have at most 50 members" and nobody is added.
3. Given a blank name, or one of 31 or more characters, when I add it, then a clear message is shown and nobody is added. Names of exactly 1 and exactly 30 characters are accepted.
4. Given "Omar" is a current member, when I add "Omar", "omar" or "OMAR", then I see "That name has already been used in this group" and nobody is added.
5. Given "Omar" is a removed member, when I add a new "Omar" (in any letter case), then I see "That name has already been used in this group" and nobody is added. The name stays Omar's, so restoring him always gives it back.
6. Given 49 current members and some removed members, when I add one more, then it succeeds, because removed members don't count toward the 50.

### US-11 View and copy the group's invite code
**As a** Group member, **I want** to see and copy my group's invite code, **so that** I can pass it to friends who want to take over their own name.
- **Job:** J8 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given I'm a current member, when I open the group's invite section, then I see the invite code and a Copy button.
2. Given I press Copy, then the code is copied, ready to paste.
3. Given any group, then there's no option to regenerate or change the invite code. It stays the same for the life of the group.

### US-12 Join a group by claiming my name
**As a** Group member, **I want** to enter a group's invite code and claim the name my friends added for me, **so that** I can see and manage my own part of the group's history.
- **Job:** J8 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given Omar creates an account and enters the group's invite code, when he chooses "I'm Omar", then his account is linked to that member, the group appears in his group list, he sees the full group history, and the activity log records "Omar claimed the name Omar".
2. Given a valid invite code and an account that isn't in the group, when I enter it, then I can choose from all of the group's **unclaimed** members, current or removed. Removed names are marked "(removed)".
3. Given a member already claimed by an account, then that name isn't offered, and no other account can claim it.
4. Given my account already claims a member in this group, then I can't claim a second member in the same group.
5. Given a valid invite code, then there's no option to add myself as a new name. Only current members add new names (US-10).
6. Given a new account claims a removed, unclaimed name, then that member is restored and linked to the account (restore limits from US-23 apply).
7. Given a wrong invite code, when I enter it, then I see "That invite code isn't valid" and join nothing.
8. Given I'm already a current member, when I enter the group's invite code, then I see "You're already in this group" and nothing changes.
9. Given a wrong code was entered, when I enter the correct code, then joining works without reloading the page.

---

## Group bills

### US-13 Record an equal-split group bill
**As a** Group member, **I want** to record a group bill split evenly between the people who took part, **so that** each pays an equal share that adds up exactly to the bill.
- **Job:** J3 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a group of 10 members, when I add a bill with 5 participants, paid by one of them, then only those 5 are charged and the other 5 members' balances don't change.
2. Given a grand total of 100.00 and 3 participants, when I press Calculate, then the shares are 33.34 / 33.33 / 33.33, the first participant in list order is marked as paying the extra cent, and the shares add up to 100.00.
3. Given food 90.00, tax 0, other charges 10% and tip 0, split between 3 participants, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 9.00, the grand total is 99.00, and each share is 33.00.
4. Given food 10.00 and other charges 0.01 (amount), split between 2 participants, then the grand total is 10.01 and the shares are 5.01 and 5.00.
5. Given a grand total of 0.01 split between 2 participants, then the shares are 0.01 and 0.00.
6. Given food 1,000,000.00, tax 0, other charges blank and a 100% tip on food, split between 50 participants, then the grand total is 2,000,000.00, each share is 40,000.00, and the shares add up to the total.
7. Given food 1,000,000.00, tax 0, other charges 1,000,000.00 (amount) and tip 0, split between 3 participants, then the grand total is 2,000,000.00 and the shares are 666,666.67 / 666,666.67 / 666,666.66.
8. Given no participants are selected, when I press Calculate, then I see "Choose who took part" and no result (no division by zero).
9. Given no items, when I press Calculate, then I see "Add at least one item" and no result.
10. Given an equal-split bill, then tax, other charges and tip follow the shared rules above, including the "tip on" option.

### US-14 Record an itemized group bill
**As a** Group member, **I want** to record which items each person had, including shared dishes, **so that** everyone pays for what they had plus a fair part of tax, other charges and tip.
- **Job:** J4 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given Ali has a 40.00 steak and Sara a 10.00 salad, with tax 5.00, other charges blank and tip 10.00, when I press Calculate, then Ali's share is 52.00 and Sara's is 13.00.
2. Given the same bill with other charges 2.50 (amount), then Ali pays 2.00 and Sara 0.50 of the other charges, Ali's share is 54.00, Sara's is 13.50, and they add up to the grand total of 67.50.
3. Given 12.00 nachos ticked for Ali, Sara and Omar, then each is charged 4.00 for the nachos.
4. Given a 10.00 item shared by 3 people, then their parts are 3.34 / 3.33 / 3.33, with the extra cent going to the first ticked person.
5. Given three participants with 10.00 of food each and other charges 0.10, then their other-charges parts are 0.04 / 0.03 / 0.03: the leftover cent goes to the first participant in list order when there's a tie.
6. Given any itemized bill, then tax, other charges and tip are each split separately in proportion to each participant's food subtotal (leftover cents by largest remainder). Each of those parts adds up exactly to the bill's tax, other charges and tip.
7. Given a participant with no items, and other charges of 5.00 on the bill, then that participant's other-charges part is 0.00, and they owe 0.00 in total (food, tax, other charges and tip).
8. Given an item with nobody ticked, when I press Calculate, then I see "Choose who shared this item" next to it and no result.
9. Given any valid itemized bill, then the per-person totals add up exactly to the grand total.
10. Given an item row, when I open its people dropdown, then it lists only this bill's participants, each with a tick box, and I can tick one or several.

## Input checks, results and saving (all bills)

### US-25 Get a clear message for every invalid input
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** a clear message next to any field I've filled in wrongly, **so that** I never get a wrong result or a crash.
- **Job:** J14 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a money field containing "abc", "-5", "1.234", "1000000.01" or a blank, when I press Calculate or Save, then a message next to that field explains the rule and no result is shown.
2. Given a money field of exactly 0.01 or exactly 1,000,000.00, then it's accepted.
3. Given tax or tip as a % outside 0–100 (e.g. -1 or 100.01), then a clear message is shown and no result.
4. Given tax or tip as a % of exactly 0 or exactly 100, then it's accepted.
5. Given a tax or tip % with more than 2 decimal places (e.g. 12.345), then a clear message is shown and no result.
6. Given tax or tip as an amount outside 0.00–1,000,000.00, or with letters or more than 2 decimals, then a clear message is shown and no result.
7. Given other charges as an amount of "abc", "-1", "0.001" or "1000000.01", then "Other charges must be between 0.01 and 1,000,000.00, or left empty" appears next to the field and no result is shown.
8. Given other charges as a % of "abc", "-5", "0.001" or "100.01", then "Other charges must be between 0.01% and 100%, or left empty" appears next to the field and no result is shown.
9. Given other charges of exactly 0.01 or 1,000,000.00 (amount), or exactly 0.01% or 100%, then it's accepted.
10. Given any bill (solo, equal or itemized) with no items, when I press Calculate, then I see "Add at least one item" and no result.
11. Given a bill with 200 items, when I add another, then I see "A bill can have at most 200 items" and no item is added.
12. Given 3 items of 1,000,000.00 each, when I press Calculate, then the food subtotal is 3,000,000.00 with no error (the limit is per field, not per total).
13. Given 200 items of 1,000,000.00 each, tax 100%, other charges 100% and tip 100% on food + tax, when I press Calculate, then the result is food 200,000,000.00, tax 200,000,000.00, other charges 200,000,000.00, tip 400,000,000.00, and grand total exactly 1,000,000,000.00.
14. Given an item name left blank, then it's shown as "Item N" by its position. An item name of exactly 40 characters is accepted, and 41 or more shows a clear message and no result.
15. Given any input at all, then the app never shows NaN, Infinity, "undefined", or a blank or crashed screen.
16. Given invalid data is sent straight to the server, bypassing the page, then the server rejects it and saves nothing.
17. Given I type "1,000.50" or "1000.50" in a money field, then both are accepted as 1000.50.
18. Given I type "1.000,50" (European style) or a misplaced comma such as "10,00", then the field's normal message is shown and no result.

## Running the app

### US-30 Run the app locally from the README
**As a** Host, **I want** to install and start the app on my computer by following the README, **so that** I can try it for free.
- **Job:** J17 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given Node.js LTS and Docker are installed, when I follow the README steps on a fresh clone (copy `.env.example` to `.env`, `docker compose up -d`, `npm install`, `npm run dev`, open the shown address), then the app runs and I can sign up locally.
2. Given the README, then it never asks for a paid account, an API key, or any third-party cloud or paid service.
3. Given the app is running, then it works with no internet-based service: accounts, data storage and calculations all happen inside the app and its own self-hosted PostgreSQL container.
4. Given the database container isn't running, when I start the app, then it prints "Can't reach the database. Start it with: docker compose up -d" and stops, with no crash trace.
5. Given a fresh database, when the app starts, then it creates its own tables automatically. No manual database setup is needed.
6. Given the database container is running, then its port is reachable only from my own computer, not from other machines on the network.
7. Given the README, then it warns that `docker compose down -v` permanently deletes all saved data, and that plain `docker compose down` keeps it.

### US-31 Deploy the app to my own server
**As a** Host, **I want** to run the same app on a server, **so that** my friends can use it for real.
- **Job:** J18 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a server with Node.js LTS and a self-hosted PostgreSQL 18 database (e.g. the same Compose file), when I deploy the same build, then it runs, configured only through settings the app owns: port, `DATABASE_URL` and session secret.
2. Given the deployed app, then it doesn't depend on any third-party cloud or paid service.
3. Given the deployed app, then passwords are stored hashed (never as plain text), and sessions use secure cookies.
4. Given the deployed app starts against a database that already has data, then pending schema updates are applied automatically and existing data is kept.

### US-32 Run all tests with one command
**As a** Host, **I want** to run every automated test with one command, **so that** I can see for myself that the app works as described.
- **Job:** J19 · **Status:** Not implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given the project is installed and the database container is running, when I run `npm test`, then the calculation, validation and server tests and the browser tests (Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, Safari's engine) all run and pass.
2. Given I have real bills saved in the app, when I run `npm test`, then the tests use only the separate test database, which is wiped and rebuilt at the start of each run, and my real data is unchanged.
3. Given I run `npm test` twice in a row, then both runs give the same results.
4. Given the database container isn't running, when I run `npm test`, then it stops at once with "Can't reach the database. Start it with: docker compose up -d".

# Communicating with the user

Users generally cannot see your thinking or any of your raw tool results. The only text the user reads is your text output, and especially your final user-facing turns after you're done working on a task. When you're writing responses for users, write short updates for a teammate that is slightly-out-of-the-loop and wants to quickly catch up. It asks only what the user must do or decide (an approval, a review request, a choice), as one question. Part of wrapping up is deciding, unasked, whether what the user asked for left a real follow-up, and where it runs; most turns leave none. One piece of work that acts on what this session just found stays here while this session has nothing else in flight ("Starting other sessions" says why): make it the box's question, with a button that has you do it here. A piece you left or could not verify is still this task, not a follow-up: finish or check it now, here or in a subagent, or name it in the recap. Any other that is a task of its own, as that section defines one (work that lands apart from this change, something the user set aside earlier, or a self-contained next task better started fresh than from a long history — never work unrelated to the request), you propose with `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` (initiation "own_initiative"; skip if you already did this turn); it shows as a New task card in the transcript, where the user starts it.

<browsers>
You have two browsers in this session:
- The built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`), also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser": a browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the user's Chrome. The built-in browser is the default for this session and its tools are already loaded, so use it unless the user asks for Claude in Chrome.
- Claude in Chrome (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`), also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser: the user's real Chrome. Use it when the user asks for it by any of these names or by describing it.
A browser is unavailable only when none of its tools are in this session (neither loaded nor deferred) or its tool calls cannot reach the browser; a blocked site, a declined approval, or a sign-in page does not make a browser unavailable. If the user asks for one browser by name and it is unavailable, say so and ask before using the other one. When a sign-in page comes up, stay in that browser; if the user says they cannot sign in to a site in the built-in browser, offer Claude in Chrome and switch only if they agree.
</browsers>

<built_in_browser>
You have a built-in browser (tools named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*`), also called the in-app browser or the browser pane: a real browser with tabs inside the Claude desktop app, isolated from the user's Chrome, with its tools already loaded. You can use it for web research, reading pages and docs, checking staging or a deployed app, filling forms, and previewing this project's dev servers. `preview_start` with a `url` opens a site in its own tab; prefer `get_page_text` / `read_page` over screenshots for reading. The user sees the same pane and can take over; they may be asked to allow a site first, and if a site is refused or declined, tell them and move on rather than retrying. Treat any sign-ins there as the user's: never sign out, change credentials, or act on an account beyond what the task needs.
</built_in_browser>

<simulator_tools>
When the user wants to run, test, or visually check an iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?"), use mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control. Simulators and emulators only — when the user asks to run on their physical device ("on my phone", "on my device"), build for the device with your normal build tools instead; these tools and the panel cannot drive a real device. Open the live panel ('attach') whenever the user would want to see the app themselves — and call 'attach' FIRST, before you build or launch: it is cheap, it opens instantly on a booted device (and surfaces the one-time device-access prompt while the user is still at the keyboard), and if nothing is booted it returns a harmless, clear error — boot or build first in that case, then attach as soon as a device is up. Do not defer the panel to the implicit re-attach in 'launch'; the panel should already be open while you build. The panel is the user's view; your own verification (screenshot, tap, text) is headless and works without it — verify yourself rather than asking the user to check. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. If 'attach' fails, follow the error's remediation: address the cause (for example no booted device, or device access not granted) or tell the user — don't retry the same call in a loop unless the error says retrying will work. If the failure is the host's Xcode setup (a wrong xcode-select, missing Xcode, or a missing iOS platform), tell the user right away with the exact fix the error gives — most of these fixes need their password, so you cannot run them (the error itself says when a fix is one you can run) — and if you continue by driving the Simulator app with generic screen tools instead, say so explicitly; never switch silently. An app in the iOS Simulator reaches a server on the machine your shell runs on at localhost, with no port forwarding.
</simulator_tools>

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. There are different types of agents that you can launch, with each type having specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Agent types which you are able to launch were given to you in a message from the system at the start of the conversation, and are supplied again if the list of available agents changes.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to choose which type of agent you want to launch. A type of "fork" forks yourself, allowing the fork to inherit your full conversation and context, and ensuring that it runs on the same model that you are running on (a `model` override is ignored for forks). For other types of subagents, they start fresh without your context window. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

There are pros and cons of delegating your work to subagents. Below we'll outline some of them to help you use your best judgement with this powerful tool.

The largest benefit in delegating to subagents is that it allows you to parallelize your work. For instance, if there is work that needs to be done by an intelligent agent such as yourself, but across (for example) several or ten or even one hundred instances of something (sets of data, parts of a codebase, servers, anything), you may want to use subagents for this work. In this case you'd want to ensure the work truly needs your intelligence, rather than being something overly simple or rote which could be done by a static script or short program. In this case your work can be significantly sped up by spinning up many agents to help you out.

The other benefit of delegation is to help you stay focused on the primary task at hand. Sometimes you will have tasks that feel like a side quest, which are not blocking you, but might help you gain some information you'd want in the future as you go about working on your primary task. For example, maybe some section of the codebase which you are not actively working on should be refactored, or maybe you want to do data analysis or set up a service which you think you'll need later, or you want to perform some important checks in the background. These are reasonable things you can outsource to a subagent so that you can remain focused on your primary task. It can be useful to think of yourself as an operator in this sense - you have entire teams of potential agents available to you all of whom are eager to help you out when you need it, and you should thus use them intelligently.

The cons of delegation are that the subagents which you launch, with the exception of a fork, only have the context that you give them. This might mean that the subagent is missing a lot of context which would help it make better decisions or produce more useful results. For this reason, when using non-fork subagents, you should provide to it as much context as possible to help it perform well. You don't have to limit the prompt to text you write yourself; you can also point subagents at any relevant documents or files whose location you know that you think would be helpful. You should make the scope clear (and generally the scope should be relatively narrow), while at the same time treating the subagent respectfully and as an intellectual peer (they are often the same model as you, just missing some context). More context and more 'why' is generally always better to provide to other agents, because this gives them more information they can use to help them exercise strong judgement, and therefore help you succeed at your task as well. Teamwork!

The other challenge of subagent usage is that you have less observability into what is happening compared to your own work, where you have full visibility into every single tool call, result, and action that occurs. Subagents run in the background, but you will be notified when one completes. If you don't yet have the results from a subagent that you launched, it is likely still running, so be sure to keep that in mind and not make up results from subagents which haven't yet finished their tasks. The subagent's final report which is given back to you when it has finished is not shown to the user - it is just shown to you, so if you want to relay something from it which is important, you have to do that yourself.

You can use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously-spawned agent with its context still intact, whereas a new Agent call starts fresh (except for fork types, which inherit your context).

Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`). Also take note that `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

In conclusion, it is best to use subagents for parallelizing your intelligence, for saving time, and for completing side-quests which do not block the main goal that you're actively working on. It is best to provide them with broad amounts of high-level context as well as their specific goals when you do use them. If the amount of work to be done is small (for example, just making a few file reads or searches or tool calls), that is probably not enough to warrant using a subagent.

For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. And once you've delegated a search, wait for the result to return rather than also running it yourself.
