questions.question:
Round 14 | Part: Groups | Targeting: Constraints | Why now: "any member can add a bill" has to work with "no paid accounts, no cloud", and that shapes the whole group feature | Ambiguity: 28.5%

The app and its saved data live on one computer. How do group members add bills?

Cause → effect:
• Shared device, no logins: whoever has the app open adds the bill and picks from the member list who paid and who was there. Members are just names, and a member "not on the app" is simply a name in the group. Effect: works fully offline, needs no accounts, and is exactly what a reviewer can test on one computer. Downside: friends can't add bills from their own phones unless they use that same computer.
• Same Wi-Fi access: the same as above, plus friends on the same Wi-Fi can open the app from their phones using the host computer's address. Still no cloud and no accounts. Effect: closer to "everyone can add", but it only works while the host computer is on and everyone is on the same network. Extra README steps, a bit more to test, and anyone on that Wi-Fi can see and edit the data.
• Real accounts for each member: each person logs in on their own device. Effect: true multi-user, but it needs an internet server, which breaks your "no cloud services" rule.

name: no-third-party-services-rule
description: What "no paid accounts, API keys or cloud services" means for the bill-splitter project — self-contained app, deployable to a server, no third-party service dependencies
metadata:
  type: project

For the bill splitting calculator, "no paid accounts, API keys or cloud services" means **the app must not depend on any third-party / external cloud or paid service**, such as hosted auth (Auth0, Firebase), hosted databases, email/SMS APIs or payment APIs. It does **not** mean the app can't be deployed: it should be a real app that can run on a server, and reviewers must still be able to run it locally by following the README.

Clarified by the user on 2026-10-21 during the requirements interview, when choosing real user accounts for groups.

**Why:** reviewers must be able to run everything themselves for free, and the product should still be deployable for real use.

**How to apply:** build accounts, storage and every other feature in-app (self-hosted auth, own database). Reject any feature that needs an outside service, such as sending email for password resets or invites, unless it can be done in-app. Keep the README's local run path working. Related: [[product-docs-requirements]].

questions.question:
Round 15 | Part: Groups | Targeting: Goal | Why now: with lasting groups, the app is either a per-bill calculator or a running record of who owes whom, and that decides most screens and stories | Ambiguity: 35%

When a group bill is added, what should the app track?

Cause → effect:
• Who paid + running balances: each bill records who paid it (e.g. Ali paid $65). The app keeps a running balance per member across all the group's bills ("Sara owes Ali $13", "Omar is owed $20"), and a "settle up" records a repayment. Effect: answers "who owes whom" after many outings, like Splitwise. Much more value, but more to build: payers, balances, settle-ups and simplified debts. Every balance must still add up to zero exactly.
• Shares only, per bill: each bill shows what each person owes for that bill, and that's it. No payer and no running totals. Effect: simpler, and every bill stands alone. But after five dinners the group has to add things up themselves.
• Shares + payer, no settle-up: records who paid and shows per-bill "X owes Y", but no running total across bills. Effect: a middle ground, but it doesn't answer the overall question either.

questions.question:
Round 16 | Part: Accounts + Groups | Targeting: Constraints | Why now: members "may or may not be on the app", and with no email service the app can't send invitations, so joining must work in-app | Ambiguity: 30.4%

How do people end up in a group?

Cause → effect:
• Name-only members + invite code to claim: any member can add a friend by name only (e.g. "Omar"), and bills and balances work for Omar right away even if he never signs up. The group has an invite code/link; when Omar creates an account and enters it, he picks "I'm Omar" and takes over that member's history. Effect: covers "may or may not be on the app" fully, with no email needed. More rules to test: claiming, and stopping two accounts from claiming the same name.
• Accounts only, with an invite code: everyone in a group must have an account, joining with the group's code. Effect: simpler and every member is a real user, but you can't add a bill for a friend who hasn't signed up yet, which breaks your "may or may not be on the app" case.
• Name-only members, never linked: friends are just names, and only the person who made the group has an account. Effect: simplest, but other members can never log in to add bills, which breaks "any member can add a bill".

options.description: Every member must sign up first. Simpler, but no members without accounts.

questions.question:
Round 17 | Part: Groups | Targeting: Success criteria | Why now: all members are equal, but editing or deleting a shared bill changes everyone's balances, so we need testable rules | Ambiguity: 25.9%

What can members change in a group?

Cause → effect:
• Everyone equal + activity log: any member can add, edit or delete any group bill or settle-up. Every change is recorded in a visible activity list ("Sara edited 'Pizza night': 60.00 → 65.00"). A member can't be removed while their balance isn't zero. Effect: matches "all members equal", and mistakes and mischief are visible to everyone. No one's balance silently disappears.
• Only the person who added a bill can edit or delete it: others can only view it. Effect: protects against accidental changes, but if that person isn't around, a mistake can't be fixed. That partly conflicts with "all members equal".
• Everyone equal, no log: anyone can change anything, and there's no record of who changed what. Effect: simplest, but balances can change with no explanation, which leads to arguments.

options.description: Members can only change bills they added themselves.

questions.question:
Round 18 | Part: Accounts | Targeting: Constraints | Why now: the no-third-party rule means the app can't send reset emails, so account recovery must work without one | Ambiguity: 23%

How should someone get back into their account if they forget their password?

Cause → effect:
• Recovery code at sign-up: when you create an account (username + password), the app shows a one-time recovery code once and asks you to save it. With that code you can set a new password. Effect: secure, needs no email, and is easy to test. If you lose both the password and the code, the account is gone (but your name in groups stays, and a new account could re-claim it via the invite code).
• Security questions: e.g. "first pet's name". Effect: familiar, but the answers are easy to guess or look up. Considered weak security today.
• No recovery: forget your password and you make a new account. Effect: simplest, but people lose their personal bill history.

Accounts use a username (not email), since email couldn't be verified without an outside service.

questions.question:
Round 19 | Part: Groups | Targeting: Goal | Why now: it's the last decision that changes every balance calculation | Ambiguity: 19.8%

Who can pay a group bill, and how are balances shown?

Cause → effect:
• One payer per bill + simplified "who pays whom": each bill has exactly one payer, chosen from the members who took part (or any group member). The balance screen shows each member's net amount (+ is owed, − owes), plus the fewest payments needed to settle everyone (e.g. "Sara pays Ali 13.00"). Effect: covers most real outings, the totals always net to exactly zero, and the payment list is short.
• Several payers per bill: e.g. Ali paid $40 and Sara paid $25 of one bill. Effect: handles split card payments at the till, but it's another set of numbers that must add up to the bill, with more errors to check and more to test.
• One payer, no simplification: shows every pairwise debt from every bill ("Sara owes Ali 13", "Ali owes Sara 5"). Effect: easier to trace back to each bill, but the list gets long and people pay each other back and forth.

options.description: One payer per bill. Balances are shown as net amounts plus the fewest payments needed to settle up.

options.label: Several payers per bill
options.description: Split payments at the till are allowed. The payer amounts must add up to the bill.

options.label: One payer, all pairwise debts
options.description: No simplification. Every debt is listed separately.

- [ ] docs/ follows the saved format rules: role/job/story templates, story → job → role links, Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and Implemented / Not implemented status.

| Assumption | Challenge | Resolution |
|------------|-----------|------------|
| Solo use is one-off | R1 | Keep a history |
| Tax/tip split equally | R2 | Proportional to food |
| History in the browser | R3 | Server-side database |
| Need three modes | R4 (contrarian) | Keep three modes |
| Rounding just works | R5 | Cent-exact, extra cents shown |
| One owner per item | R6 (simplifier) | Shared items allowed |
| One way to enter tax/tip | R7 | % or amount for each |
| No limits needed | R8 | Explicit limits; currency per group/bill, locked |
| Saved bills fixed | R9 | View, edit, delete |
| Stack open | R10 | TypeScript everywhere |
| Live results | R11 | Calculate button; stale results hidden |
| Tip base fixed | R12 | Per-bill option, food only by default |
| Groups are one-off splits | R13 (ontologist) | Lasting groups, equal members, subset bills |
| "No cloud" means local only | R14 | No third-party services; deployable; real accounts |
| Bills split once and forgotten | R15 | Payer + running balances + settle-up |
| Everyone must have an account | R16 | Name-only members, claimable by invite code |
| Need an admin | R17 | Everyone equal + activity log |
| Email reset needed | R18 | One-time recovery code |
| Several payers needed | R19 | One payer + simplified settle-up |

- **Language:** TypeScript (frontend and backend), with a shared pure calculation module that works in integer cents and is used by both the page and the server.
- **Frontend:** React built with Vite. **Backend:** Node.js LTS + Express, serving the API and the built frontend from one process (easy to deploy).
- **Database:** SQLite file; prefer Node's built-in `node:sqlite` so no native build step is needed.
- **Auth:** password hashing with Node's built-in `crypto.scrypt`, server-side sessions in an httpOnly, SameSite cookie, and login rate limiting done in-app.
- **Tests:** Vitest (calculation, validation and API) and Playwright (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit).
- **Layout:** `src/` (client, server, shared), `tests/`, `docs/`, `transcripts/`, README.

| Entity | Type | Fields | Relationships |
|--------|------|--------|---------------|
| Account | core | username, passwordHash, recoveryCodeHash | owns SoloBills; claims Members |
| Group | core | name, currency, inviteCode | has Members, GroupBills, SettleUps, ActivityEntries |
| Member | core | displayName, accountId? (null = name-only) | belongs to Group; participant/payer in GroupBills |
| SoloBill | core | name, currency, items, tax, tip, tipBase | belongs to Account |
| GroupBill | core | name, splitMode (equal/itemized), payer, participants, items, tax, tip, tipBase | belongs to Group |
| Item | core | name, priceCents, sharers | belongs to a bill |
| Share | derived | memberId, food/tax/tip/total cents, extraCent | computed per participant |
| SettleUp | core | from, to, amountCents, date | belongs to Group |
| Balance | derived | memberId, netCents | computed from GroupBills + SettleUps |
| SuggestedPayment | derived | from, to, amountCents | computed from Balances |
| ActivityEntry | supporting | who, when, action, before/after | belongs to Group |
| Currency, Tax, Tip | supporting | symbol; mode + value | on Group/bills |

## Ontology Convergence
| Round | Entity Count | New | Stable | Stability Ratio |
|-------|-------------|-----|--------|----------------|
| 1 | 6 | 6 | - | - |
| 5 | 10 | 1 | 9 | 90% |
| 10 | 11 | 0 | 11 | 100% |
| 13 | 12 | 1 (Group) | 10 + 1 renamed (Person→Member) | 83% → reframed |
| 14 | 13 | 1 (Account) | 12 | 85% |
| 15 | 15 | 2 (SettleUp, Balance) | 13 | 87% |
| 17 | 16 | 1 (ActivityEntry) | 15 | 94% |
| 19 | 17 | 1 (SuggestedPayment) | 16 | 94% |

## Open Assumptions (confirm while planning, low risk)
- The payer can be any current group member, even one who didn't take part in the bill.
- A settle-up can be any valid amount, even more than is owed, and the balances simply update.
- Removed members (balance 0) stay visible on their old bills, marked "(removed)".
- Any member can view and regenerate the group's invite code.
- There's no group-less quick split: a one-off group outing means creating a group.

<summary>Q&A summary (19 rounds)</summary>

- **R0** 5 components confirmed (Groups and Accounts were added later).
- **R1** Solo: **keep history** · **R2** Tax/tip: **proportional** · **R3** Storage: **server + database**

- **R11** **Calculate button** · **R12** Tip base: **user chooses per bill**
- **R13** Roles: Solo diner + equal Group members; lasting groups; bills for a subset of members (ambiguity rose to 28.5%)

- **R15** **Payer + running balances** (30.4%) · **R16** **Name-only members + invite code to claim** (25.9%)
- **R17** **Everyone equal + activity log** (23%) · **R18** **Recovery code** (19.8%) · **R19** **One payer + simplified settle-up** (17.6%)
</details>

### History (AC-H)
- [ ] Given I save a solo bill, then it appears at the top of my history with name, date, currency and total. The name is optional and defaults to "Bill – date".
- [ ] Given a saved solo bill, I can open it, edit it (with the same validation and recalculation as a new bill, and the currency locked) and delete it after a confirmation.
- [ ] Given the server restarts, then all bills, groups and balances are still there.

### Tech & setup (AC-T)
- [ ] With Node.js LTS installed, a fresh clone plus the README steps (install, start, open URL) gives a working app, and I can sign up locally. No outside service, key or account is needed.

### Product docs (AC-D)

## Roles (for docs)
- **Solo diner:** eats or shops alone and wants an accurate personal total and a private record of spending. Must never see other people's bills, or have their solo bills seen by anyone else.
- **Group member:** belongs to one or more friend groups, all with equal rights. Can add, edit or delete group bills and settle-ups, add name-only friends, and see balances. Must never see groups they aren't in, remove a member who still owes or is owed, or change a group's currency.
- Friends who never sign up exist only as **name-only members**. They are data, not a role.

## Assumptions Exposed & Resolved
| Assumption | Challenge | Resolution |
|------------|-----------|------------|
| Solo use is one-off | R1 | Keep a history |
| Tax/tip split equally | R2 | Proportional to food |
| History in the browser | R3 | Server-side database |
| Need three modes | R4 (contrarian) | Keep three modes |
| Rounding just works | R5 | Cent-exact, extra cents shown |

| Tip base fixed | R12 | Per-bill option, food only by default |

| "No cloud" means local only | R14 | No third-party services; deployable; real accounts |
| Bills split once and forgotten | R15 | Payer + running balances + settle-up |
| Everyone must have an account | R16 | Name-only members, claimable by invite code |
| Need an admin | R17 | Everyone equal + activity log |
| Email reset needed | R18 | One-time recovery code |
| Several payers needed | R19 | One payer + simplified settle-up |

## Technical Context
- **Language:** TypeScript (frontend and backend), with a shared pure calculation module that works in integer cents and is used by both the page and the server.
- **Frontend:** React built with Vite. **Backend:** Node.js LTS + Express, serving the API and the built frontend from one process (easy to deploy).
- **Database:** SQLite file; prefer Node's built-in `node:sqlite` so no native build step is needed.
- **Auth:** password hashing with Node's built-in `crypto.scrypt`, server-side sessions in an httpOnly, SameSite cookie, and login rate limiting done in-app.
- **Tests:** Vitest (calculation, validation and API) and Playwright (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit).
- **Layout:** `src/` (client, server, shared), `tests/`, `docs/`, `transcripts/`, README.

| SuggestedPayment | derived | from, to, amountCents | computed from Balances |
| ActivityEntry | supporting | who, when, action, before/after | belongs to Group |

content.text:
I've sent you the spec file above. It's saved at [.omc/specs/deep-interview-bill-splitter.md](.omc/specs/deep-interview-bill-splitter.md). Nothing has been built yet.

**What's in it:**
- **The app:** solo diners track their own bills privately. Friends form lasting groups where any member can add a bill, choose who paid and who took part, and split it equally or by items. Shared dishes are allowed.
- **Money rules:** all math is exact to the cent, and shares always add up to the bill. Tax and tip can each be a % or an amount, and the tip base is chosen per bill. Each group has one currency symbol that can't be changed.
- **Groups:** running balances, the fewest payments needed to settle up, and recorded settle-ups. All members are equal and every change is logged. Friends can be added by name and claim their spot later with an invite code.
- **Accounts:** username and password, with a one-time recovery code instead of email.
- **Limits and errors:** amounts from 0.01 to 1,000,000, groups of 2–50 people, and tax/tip from 0–100%. Every bad input gets a clear message, and results only appear when you press Calculate.
- **Tech:** TypeScript, React, Node.js/Express and SQLite. It runs locally from the README with only Node.js installed, and can be deployed to any server.
- **Acceptance criteria:** Given/When/Then checks for each part, ready to become your user stories.

**Saved to memory:** what "no cloud services" means here. The app can't depend on outside or paid services, but it can be deployed to a server.

**Still open:** five small assumptions, listed near the end of the spec, such as whether someone who didn't eat can be the payer. They're easy to confirm before building.

The `.omc` folder is gitignored, so the spec is on your computer but not in your repo.

questions.question:
Each bill has a 'tip on' option (food only / food + tax). Should the tip ever be calculated on other charges too?
• Never: the tip options stay 'food only' and 'food + tax'. Other charges (e.g. service or delivery fees) are not tipped on.
• Add a third option: 'food + tax + other charges'. More flexible, but one more case to test.

options.label: Never tip on other charges (Recommended)
options.description: Tip options stay food only (default) or food + tax.

options.label: Add third tip option
options.description: Tip on: food only / food + tax / food + tax + other charges.

questions.question:
In an itemized group split, how are other charges shared between participants?
• Proportional to food, like tax and tip: someone who ordered 80% of the food pays 80% of other charges.
• Split equally between all participants: suits fixed fees such as a table or delivery fee, but the person who ate less pays relatively more.

options.label: Proportional to food (Recommended)
options.description: Same rule as tax and tip. Leftover cents by largest remainder.

options.label: Split equally
options.description: Each participant pays the same share of other charges. Leftover cents go to the first participants.

content.text:
The spec now includes the **Other charges** field everywhere a bill's money is described: [deep-interview-bill-splitter.md](.omc/specs/deep-interview-bill-splitter.md) (now v2.1).

**The rules, from your answers:**
- **Where it applies:** every bill has it, solo and both group modes. It's one field labelled "Other charges", with a % / amount switch like tax and tip.
- **Allowed values:** it's optional, and blank or 0 means none (the result then shows "Other charges 0.00"). As an amount it's 0.01–1,000,000.00, and as a % it's 0.01–100. Both allow at most 2 decimals.
- **What the % is of:** the food subtotal only, never tax or tip.
- **No tax or tip on it:** tax is never charged on other charges, and a tip is never calculated on them, whichever tip option is chosen.
- **Itemized bills:** other charges are split in proportion to each person's food, like tax and tip. Leftover cents go by largest remainder, and ties go to the first person in the list.
- **Totals:** grand total = food + tax + other charges + tip, and this is what an equal split divides.

**Spec sections I updated:**
- the main-parts table and the goal
- the limits
- a new non-goals entry: no extra charge lines, and no tax or tip on other charges
- the calculation rules: three new rules (other charges, rounding order, grand-total formula), with the rest renumbered 1–10
- the ontology tables
- the assumptions table and the transcript

**New acceptance criteria:**
- solo bills: % and amount, the "food only" base, half-up rounding, 0 meaning none, and the 1,000,000 maximum
- equal splits: three new cases
- itemized splits: three new cases, including the tie on a leftover cent
- error messages for bad amount and % values
- the old result being hidden after switching between % and amount
- reopening a saved bill with other charges

**Checks:**
- I recalculated every new example with a script, and they all add up (for example 26.00, 134.00, 54.00 / 13.50, 5.01 / 5.00).
- I searched for leftover tax and tip mentions. Only one example needed fixing, the 1,000,000 case, which didn't say what other charges was set to.
- I listed one new open assumption at the end of the spec. Tax and tip % precision was never specified, so I assumed 2 decimals to match other charges.

questions.question:
First, what 'removed' means. A member with balance 0.00 is just settled: they're still in the group and nothing changes. 'Removed' means someone took them OUT of the group's member list (the spec already says this is only allowed once their balance is 0.00). The question is what happens to the old bills they were part of.

Example: Omar was on 'Pizza night' (paid 30.00, his share 10.00). Later he settles up and is removed.
• Keep on old bills, marked: 'Pizza night' still shows 'Omar (removed)' as payer and participant. All totals and other members' balances stay exactly the same. Omar can't be picked for new bills.
• Keep on old bills, no mark: the same, but his name shows normally, so it's unclear he's no longer in the group.
• Delete from old bills too: Omar disappears everywhere. His 30.00 payment and 10.00 share would vanish, changing 'Pizza night' and everyone's balances, so old balances become wrong. (Not recommended: breaks the 'never a wrong result' rule.)
• Don't allow removing anyone who appears on any bill: members can only be removed if they were never on a bill.

options.label: Keep, marked (removed) (Recommended)
options.description: Old bills and balances unchanged. The name shows as 'Omar (removed)'. Can't be picked for new bills.

options.label: Keep, no mark
options.description: Old bills unchanged and the name shown normally. Can't be picked for new bills.

options.label: Only remove if never on a bill
options.description: Anyone who appears on any bill can never be removed.

options.label: Delete from old bills
options.description: Erases their part of past bills, which changes everyone's balances.

questions.question:
If a removed member comes back (e.g. Omar rejoins the friend group), what should happen?
• Restore the same member: any member can restore Omar, his old history reconnects, and the '(removed)' mark goes away.
• Add as a new member: a fresh 'Omar' is added, and his old bills stay with the removed one. Simpler, but his history is split in two.
• No coming back: removal is permanent.

options.label: Restore same member (Recommended)
options.description: Any member can restore them. One continuous history, and the mark disappears.

options.label: Add as new member
options.description: Old history stays with the removed entry.

options.label: Permanent
options.description: A removed member can never return.

questions.question:
When the removed member had an account (they had claimed their name), what happens to that account?
• Loses access: the group disappears from their list, and they can no longer open its bills or balances. Their account and solo bills are untouched.
• Read-only access: they can still view the group's history but can't add or change anything.

options.label: Loses access (Recommended)
options.description: The group disappears for them. Their account and solo bills are untouched.

options.label: Read-only access
options.description: They can still view the group's history but not change it.

questions.question:
Can a member remove themselves (leave the group)?
• Yes, same rules: anyone can leave once their own balance is 0.00. It's then the same as being removed, and the activity log records 'Omar left'.
• No: only other members can remove them.

options.label: Yes, at balance 0.00 (Recommended)
options.description: Leaving follows the same rules as removal, and the activity log records it.

options.label: No self-leave
options.description: Only other members can remove someone.

input.new_string:
- Each group bill has one payer, and **the payer must be one of that bill's participants**. The payer list only offers ticked participants. If the payer is unticked, Calculate and Save show "The payer must be one of the people on this bill".
   - The payer is credited with the full grand total, and each participant (including the payer) is debited their share. So the payer's net change is grand total − their own share.
   - A settle-up from A to B (A pays B) credits A and debits B. A and B must be two different current members. The amount can be any valid amount (0.01–1,000,000.00, 2 decimals), **even more than A owes B**. The balances simply update, and an overpayment flips the direction of the debt.

content.text:
The spec is updated with all four of your decisions (now v2.2): [deep-interview-bill-splitter.md](.omc/specs/deep-interview-bill-splitter.md).

**What changed:**
- **Payer:** must be one of the bill's participants. The payer list only offers ticked people, and unticking the payer shows "The payer must be one of the people on this bill".
- **Settle-ups:** can be any amount from 0.01 to 1,000,000.00, even more than is owed. Example: Sara owes Ali 13.00 and pays 20.00, so now Ali owes Sara 7.00.
- **Invite code:** created automatically with the group and never changes. There's no regenerate option. Any member can view it and copy it with a Copy button.
- **Removed members:**
  - **Settled is not removed.** A member with balance 0.00 is still a normal member. "Removed" means taken off the member list, which is only allowed at 0.00.
  - They stay on old bills as "Omar (removed)", and no totals or balances change.
  - They can't be picked for new bills or settle-ups.
  - Any member can **restore** them, with their full history.
  - A removed member with an account **loses access** to the group. Their account and solo bills are untouched.
  - Members can **leave** on their own once their balance is 0.00.
  - The activity log records removals, leaving and restores.

**Rules I added to close gaps:**
1. **Bills that include a removed member are view-only** until that member is restored. Editing them would change the balance of someone who's no longer in the group.
2. **The last member with an account can't leave or be removed.** Otherwise a group could end up with nobody able to log in.
3. **The invite code can't be used to get back in after removal.** It only lets someone claim an unclaimed, current name, so a removed person needs a current member to restore them.
4. **Group size is now 1–50 current members, instead of "2–50".** A group starts with only its creator, so "2–50" contradicted the group-creation rule.
5. **A settle-up must be between two different current members.**

Two open assumptions remain from before: there's no quick split without a group, and tax and tip % accept up to 2 decimals.

questions.question:
When the last member with an account leaves, you'd like a warning. After they confirm, what happens to the group?
• Deleted for good: the warning says "You're the last member with an account. If you leave, this group and all its bills, settle-ups and history will be permanently deleted." Leave → the group is gone; Cancel → nothing changes. Clear and simple to test.
• Kept but frozen: the group stays in the database with nobody able to open it, until someone claims a name with the invite code. Data is never lost, but there's an invisible group nobody can reach.

options.label: Deleted for good (Recommended)
options.description: Warning, then on Leave the group and all its data are permanently deleted. Cancel keeps everything.

options.label: Kept but frozen
options.description: The group stays, unreachable until someone claims a name with the invite code.

questions.question:
Must the last member with an account settle to 0.00 before leaving (and deleting the group)?
• No: the group and everyone's balances are deleted anyway, so the warning just also says "Unsettled balances will be lost".
• Yes: same rule as everyone else. They must be at 0.00 before they can leave, even though the group then disappears.

options.label: No, warn instead (Recommended)
options.description: They can leave at any balance. The warning mentions unsettled balances will be lost.

options.label: Yes, 0.00 first
options.description: The same balance rule as all members.

• Code brings removed members back: if Omar enters the code, he's restored automatically with his full history (the same as a member pressing Restore). The log says "Omar rejoined with the invite code". The code still also lets new people claim unclaimed names.
• Code brings people back AND lets anyone add themselves: the same, plus someone whose name isn't on the list can add themselves as a brand-new member. Most open, but anyone with the code can join.
• Code only claims names (as before), and removed people come back only through Restore. (This is the rule you said you don't need.)

options.label: Also restores removed (Recommended)
options.description: Entering the code restores a removed member automatically, and new people can still claim unclaimed names.

options.label: Restores + self-add new
options.description: Also lets anyone with the code add themselves as a new member.

**Last member with an account leaving:**
- They're no longer blocked. When they press Leave, they see: "You're the last member with an account. If you leave, this group and all its bills, settle-ups and history will be permanently deleted. Unsettled balances will be lost."

- The group disappears for everyone, its address shows "This group no longer exists", and its invite code stops working.
- Accounts, solo bills and other groups are never affected.

**Invite code:**
- The old restriction is gone. If a removed member enters the code, they're restored automatically with their full history and access, and the log records "Omar rejoined with the invite code".

**Two small rules I added:**
1. A new account entering the code can claim any unclaimed name, including removed ones, which are marked "(removed)". Claiming a removed name brings it back.
2. There's no separate "delete group" button. A group is only deleted when its last member with an account leaves.

I also searched the spec for old wording that conflicts with these changes, and none is left.

34	## Goal
35	A self-contained web app for splitting and tracking bills:
36	- **Solo diners** total their own bills (items, tax, other charges and tip) and keep a private history.
37	- **Friends** form lasting groups. Any member can record a group bill: who paid, who took part, and whether it's split equally or by items. The app keeps exact running balances, shows the fewest payments needed to settle up, and records settle-ups.
38	
39	All money math is exact to the cent, and every invalid input gives a clear message, never a crash or a wrong result.
40	
41	## Constraints
42	- **Browsers:** current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari.
43	- **No third-party services:** the app must not depend on any external cloud or paid service (no hosted auth, hosted database, email/SMS or payment APIs). It **can** be deployed to a server. Reviewers must be able to run it locally from the README with only free software (Node.js LTS).
44	- **Accounts:** built into the app. Username + password, with passwords hashed. Sessions use secure cookies. No email anywhere.
45	- **Storage:** SQLite database file managed by the app's own server.
46	- **Modes:** Solo (personal), Group bill with Equal split, and Group bill with Itemized split. These are separate screens and rules (Round 4).
47	- **Number limits:**
48	  - Money: 0.01–1,000,000.00, at most 2 decimal places. No negatives, letters, blanks or extra decimals.
49	  - Group size: 1–50 **current** members. A group starts with just its creator, and removed members don't count toward the 50.
50	  - Tax and tip %: 0–100, at most 2 decimal places (e.g. 12.5 or 8.25). Tax and tip amounts: 0.00–1,000,000.00.
51	  - Other charges (optional): blank, 0 or 0.00 means "no other charges". Otherwise:
52	    - as an amount: 0.01–1,000,000.00, at most 2 decimal places
53	    - as a %: 0.01–100, at most 2 decimal places
54	    - negatives, letters and extra decimals are rejected.
55	- **Bill fields:** every bill (solo and both group modes) has the same four money parts: items, tax, **other charges** and tip. Other charges is a single field per bill, always labelled "Other charges" (for service, delivery or table fees and similar), with a % / amount switch like tax and tip.
56	- **Currency:** a display symbol only, picked from a fixed list (e.g. $, €, £, ¥, ₹, Rs), with no conversion.
57	  - Each **group** has one currency, chosen at creation and never changeable. A note says so when you choose it.
58	  - Each **solo bill** has its own currency, locked when the bill is first saved.
59	- **Math:** integer cents only, never floating-point money.
60	- **Results:** totals appear when the user presses **Calculate**. Changing any input hides the old result until Calculate is pressed again.
61	
62	## Non-Goals
63	- Currency conversion; multiple currencies in one group.
64	- Email or SMS (invites, password resets, notifications).
65	- Real payment processing (settle-ups are records only).
66	- Receipt scanning, native mobile apps, real-time push updates.
67	- Multiple payers on one bill (Round 19).
68	- Regenerating or changing a group's invite code.
69	- A quick split without a group: splitting a bill between people always happens inside a group, even for a one-off outing.
70	- Permanently deleting a member, or erasing their part of past bills.
71	- More than one other-charges line per bill, or custom labels for it.
72	- Tax on other charges, or tip on other charges.

74	## Calculation Rules
75	1. **Tax:** a % (of the food subtotal) or an amount. Tax is never charged on other charges or tip.
76	2. **Other charges:** optional; a % or an amount. A % is a percentage of the **food subtotal only** (the same base as tax), never of tax or tip. Blank or 0 means 0.00 other charges, and the results still show an "Other charges 0.00" line.
77	3. **Tip:** a % or an amount. Tip may be 0. For a % tip, each bill has a "tip on" option: **food only (default)** or **food + tax**. Neither option includes other charges: a tip is never calculated on other charges.
78	4. **Rounding and order:** tax, other charges and tip are each worked out separately, in cents. Any % result is rounded half-up to the cent, so it can be 0.00 (e.g. 5% of 0.01). A "food + tax" tip uses the already-rounded tax.
79	5. **Grand total** = food subtotal + tax + other charges + tip.
80	6. **Equal split:** grand total (including other charges) ÷ number of participants. Leftover cents go 1 each to the first participants in list order, and the app shows who pays the extra cent.
81	7. **Itemized split:**
82	   - Each item has a price and 1+ ticked participants. Its cost is split evenly between them, with leftover cents going to the first ticked people.
83	   - Tax, other charges and tip are each split separately in proportion to each participant's food subtotal. Leftover cents are assigned by largest remainder, and ties go to the first participant in list order.
84	   - A participant with no items owes 0.00 (including 0.00 tax, other charges and tip).
85	8. **Group balances:**
86	   - Each group bill has one payer, and **the payer must be one of that bill's participants**. The payer list only offers ticked participants. If the payer is unticked, Calculate and Save show "The payer must be one of the people on this bill".
87	   - The payer is credited with the full grand total, and each participant (including the payer) is debited their share. So the payer's net change is grand total − their own share.
88	   - A settle-up from A to B (A pays B) credits A and debits B. A and B must be two different current members. The amount can be any valid amount (0.01–1,000,000.00, 2 decimals), **even more than A owes B**. The balances simply update, and an overpayment flips the direction of the debt.
89	   - Net balances across the group always sum to exactly 0.00.
90	9. **Invite code:**
91	   - Each group gets one invite code, generated automatically when the group is created. It never changes, and there is no regenerate option.
92	   - Any current member can view it and copy it with a Copy button.
93	   - Entering the code (while logged in) does one of the following:
94	     - **Removed member with this account:** they are **restored automatically** with their full history (the same as Restore). The log says "Omar rejoined with the invite code".
95	     - **New account:** they choose a name to claim from the group's **unclaimed** members, current or removed. Removed names are marked "(removed)", and claiming one restores it.
96	     - **Already a current member:** "You're already in this group", and nothing changes.
97	   - The code can't create a brand-new member. New names are added by a current member.
98	   - The restore limits below (50 current members, no duplicate current name) apply to rejoining with the code too.
99	10. **Removing, leaving and restoring members:**
100	   - **Settled ≠ removed.** A member with balance 0.00 is still a normal member. "Removed" means taken off the group's current member list.
101	   - Any member can remove another member, and any member can leave (remove themselves), but **only when that member's balance is exactly 0.00**. The one exception is the last member with an account, below.
102	   - **Last member with an account leaving:** when the only current member with an account presses Leave, the app warns: "You're the last member with an account. If you leave, this group and all its bills, settle-ups and history will be permanently deleted. Unsettled balances will be lost."
103	     - **Cancel:** nothing changes.
104	     - **Leave:** the whole group is permanently deleted, including its members, bills, settle-ups, activity log and invite code. Their balance doesn't need to be 0.00 first.
105	     - This only happens through leaving. Anyone else removing them would themselves have to be a current member with an account, so they could never be the last one.
106	   - Leaving or deleting never touches anyone's account or solo bills.
107	   - There is no separate "delete group" button.
108	   - Removing never changes past data. Old bills and settle-ups keep the member, shown as "Name (removed)", and every total and balance stays exactly the same.
109	   - A removed member can't be chosen as payer, participant or settle-up person on new bills or settle-ups. They don't appear in the balance list or the settle-up suggestions.
110	   - While a member is removed, any bill or settle-up that includes them is **view-only**: it can't be edited or deleted, because that would change a removed member's balance. The message is "Restore Omar to change this bill".
111	   - If the removed member had an account, they **lose access** to the group right away: it disappears from their group list, and its pages are refused even by typing the address directly. Their account and solo bills are untouched, and the link between their account and the member is kept.
112	   - The group's members page lists removed members under "Removed members", each with a **Restore** button that any current member can use. Restoring brings back the same member, with one continuous history and the "(removed)" mark gone. If they had an account, their access returns.
113	   - Restoring is refused with a clear message if the group already has 50 current members, or if a current member already has the same name.
114	   - The activity log records "X removed Omar", "Omar left", "X restored Omar" and "Omar rejoined with the invite code".
115	11. **Settle-up suggestions:** the fewest payments that bring every net balance to zero (greedy match of largest debtor to largest creditor), shown as "X pays Y amount".
116	12. **Invariant:** for every bill, the shares sum exactly to the grand total. In itemized bills, the per-person tax, other-charges and tip parts also each sum exactly to the bill's tax, other charges and tip.

223	- **Solo diner:** eats or shops alone and wants an accurate personal total and a private record of spending. Must never see other people's bills, or have their solo bills seen by anyone else.

255	## Technical Context
256	- **Language:** TypeScript (frontend and backend), with a shared pure calculation module that works in integer cents and is used by both the page and the server.
257	- **Frontend:** React built with Vite. **Backend:** Node.js LTS + Express, serving the API and the built frontend from one process (easy to deploy).
258	- **Database:** SQLite file; prefer Node's built-in `node:sqlite` so no native build step is needed.
259	- **Auth:** password hashing with Node's built-in `crypto.scrypt`, server-side sessions in an httpOnly, SameSite cookie, and login rate limiting done in-app.
260	- **Tests:** Vitest (calculation, validation and API) and Playwright (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit).
261	- **Layout:** `src/` (client, server, shared), `tests/`, `docs/`, `transcripts/`, README.

# App Roles

Who uses the Bill Splitting Calculator. Each role is a different kind of person with different needs. Jobs are in [jobs-to-be-done.md](jobs-to-be-done.md), and stories are in [user-stories.md](user-stories.md).

## Solo diner

A **Solo diner** is someone who eats out, orders in or shops on their own and pays their own bill. They want to know the exact amount to pay, including tax, any other charges (such as a service, delivery or table fee) and tip, and they want a private record of what they've spent.

They can:
- create an account with a username and password, receive a one-time recovery code, log in, and reset a forgotten password with that code
- enter a bill's items, tax, other charges and tip, each of tax, other charges and tip as a % or an amount, and choose whether a % tip is on the food only or on the food + tax
- pick the bill's currency symbol, press Calculate and see the subtotal, tax, other charges, tip and total, exact to the cent
- save the bill to their personal history, then reopen, edit or delete saved bills

They must never:
- see another person's solo bills, or have their own solo bills seen or changed by anyone else, even by typing a page address directly
- change a solo bill's currency once that bill has been saved
- be shown a wrong, stale or broken result (such as NaN, Infinity or "undefined") for any input

## Group member

A **Group member** belongs to one or more lasting groups of friends who share costs again and again: meals, trips, groceries. Every member has equal rights; there is no admin or organizer. A bill may involve the whole group or only the members who took part, and one person usually pays the bill for everyone. They want to know, at any time, who owes whom across all the group's bills, and the fewest payments needed to settle up.

They can:
- create a group with a name and a currency, and add friends to it by name, even friends who never create an account
- view the group's invite code and copy it, and use an invite code to join a group by claiming their name, or to rejoin a group they were removed from
- record a group bill: choose who took part, who paid (one of the people who took part) and whether to split it equally or by items, with shared items split between the people who had them
- see every member's running balance and the suggested payments to settle up, and record settle-ups (repayments) of any valid amount
- add, edit or delete any group bill or settle-up, and see every change in the group's activity log
- remove a member whose balance is 0.00, leave the group when their own balance is 0.00, and restore removed members
- as the last member with an account, leave after a warning, which permanently deletes the group

They must never:
- see or open a group they don't belong to, including a group they've been removed from
- remove another member, or leave themselves, while that member's balance isn't 0.00. The one exception is the last member with an account leaving, which deletes the group after a warning.
- record a bill whose payer isn't one of the people who took part in it
- edit or delete a bill or settle-up that includes a removed member, until that member is restored
- change the group's currency after the group is created
- create a brand-new member by entering an invite code; only current members add new names

## Host

A **Host** is someone who installs and runs their own copy of the app. This is either a reviewer checking the project on their own computer, or someone running it on a server so their friends can use it. They don't need to know how the app works inside, but they need it to start reliably by following the README, with nothing to buy or sign up for.

They can:
- install it with only free software (Node.js LTS) and start it by following the README
- run it on a server, configured only through settings the app owns (port, database file location, session secret)
- run all of the app's automated tests with one command

They must never:
- need a paid account, an API key or any third-party cloud or paid service to install, run, test or deploy the app

## How the roles differ

| Need | Solo diner | Group member | Host |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main question | "What do I owe for this bill?" | "Who owes whom across all our bills?" | "Does it run and work as promised?" |
| Who sees the data | Only them | Only the group's current members | Doesn't use bill data |
| Splitting | None, one person pays everything | Equal or by items, among the people who took part | — |
| Payer and balances | Not needed | One payer per bill, running balances, settle-ups | — |
| Changing records | Their own bills only | Any group bill or settle-up, with every change logged | — |
| Account needed | Yes | Yes, to log in; friends without accounts appear as name-only members | No app account needed to install or run |

## Notes

- **One person can hold several roles.** The same account can keep solo bills (Solo diner) and belong to groups (Group member).
- **Name-only members are not a role.** Friends who never sign up exist only as names inside a group. They can be chosen as a participant, and as the payer of bills they took part in, but they never use the app themselves unless they later create an account and claim their name.

# Jobs to Be Done

Why people use the Bill Splitting Calculator. Each job is something the person needs to get done whether or not this app exists, so no job mentions the app, its screens or its buttons. Each job names the role it belongs to (see [app-roles.md](app-roles.md)), and every story in [user-stories.md](user-stories.md) names the job it serves.

## Solo diner

**J1. Know exactly what I owe**
When I've finished a meal or a purchase on my own and the bill adds tax, extra fees and a tip, I want to know the exact amount to pay, to the cent, so I can pay the right amount without doing the maths in my head.
- Role: Solo diner

**J2. Keep a record of my own spending**
When I look back at what I've spent on meals and purchases, I want an accurate record of each past bill that I can correct or remove, so I can keep track of my spending and trust the numbers.
- Role: Solo diner

## Group member

**J3. Share a bill evenly**
When a group of us shares one bill and we agree to split it evenly, I want each person's share worked out so that the shares add up to exactly the bill, so I can make sure nobody pays a cent too much or too little.
- Role: Group member

**J4. Pay for what each person had**
When a group of us orders different things, including dishes some of us share, I want each person to pay for what they had plus a fair part of the tax, fees and tip, so I can make the split fair to people who ordered less.
- Role: Group member

**J5. Charge only the people who were there**
When one friend pays for an outing that only some of our friend group joined, I want to note who paid and who took part, so I can make sure only the people who were there owe a share and the person who paid gets it back.
- Role: Group member

**J6. Know who owes whom overall**
When my friends and I share costs again and again over weeks or months, I want to know at any moment what each person owes or is owed in total, and the fewest payments that would square everyone up, so I can settle debts without long lists of back-and-forth payments.
- Role: Group member

**J7. Count repayments**
When one friend pays another back, I want that repayment taken off what they owed, even if they pay back more than they owed, so I can keep everyone's running totals correct.
- Role: Group member

**J8. Include friends who don't keep records**
When some friends in our circle don't keep their own records of shared costs, I want to include them in our shared costs from the start and let them take over their own part whenever they choose to, so I can keep everyone's history complete.
- Role: Group member

**J9. See who changed what**
When anyone in our group adds, changes or removes a shared cost or a repayment, I want to see who did it, when, and what changed, so I can trust the totals and sort out disagreements.
- Role: Group member

**J10. Keep history right when people leave or come back**
When someone leaves our circle of friends, or comes back later, I want their past share to stay exactly as it was and their access to our shared records to end or return with them, so I can keep our history correct and keep it private to the people currently in the group.
- Role: Group member

**J11. Close out a group for good**
When I'm the last person still keeping a group's shared records and we're finished with them, I want to close them out completely, so I can leave nothing behind.
- Role: Group member

## Solo diner and Group member

**J12. Keep my money records private**
When I keep records of what I've spent, paid or am owed, I want only me, or only the friends a record concerns, to be able to see or change them, so I can trust that nobody else reads or alters my financial details.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J13. Get back in without help**
When I forget the secret I use to protect my records, I want a way to regain access that doesn't depend on anyone else, so I can make sure I never lose my history.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J14. Catch mistakes before relying on a figure**
When I'm working out money amounts and I make a typing mistake or enter something impossible, I want the mistake caught and clearly explained before I rely on the result, so I can never pay or charge someone the wrong amount.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J15. See amounts in my own currency**
When I pay in a particular currency, I want amounts shown with that currency's symbol and kept in one currency throughout, so I can read every figure without confusion.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J16. Use the browser I already have**
When I need to work out or check a bill, I want to do it in whichever common, up-to-date web browser I already use, so I can avoid installing or buying anything extra.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

## Host

**J17. Try it on my own computer for free**
When I want to try out or review a piece of software, I want to install and run my own copy on my computer with only free tools and no outside accounts or services, so I can evaluate it without paying or signing up for anything.
- Role: Host

**J18. Run it on my own server**
When I want my friends to use a tool for real, I want to run it on a server I control, without depending on any third-party company's services, so I can keep it running and keep our data with us.
- Role: Host

**J19. Get proof that it works**
When I evaluate a piece of software, I want quick, repeatable proof that it behaves as described in the common web browsers, so I can trust its claims without checking everything by hand.
- Role: Host

When I'm working out money amounts and I make a typing mistake or enter something impossible, I want the mistake caught and clearly explained before I rely on the result, so I can never pay or charge someone the wrong amount.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J15. See amounts in my own currency**
When I pay in a particular currency, I want amounts shown with that currency's symbol and kept in one currency throughout, so I can read every figure without confusion.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

**J16. Use the browser I already have**
When I need to work out or check a bill, I want to do it in whichever common, up-to-date web browser I already use, so I can avoid installing or buying anything extra.
- Roles: Solo diner, Group member

## Host

**J17. Try it on my own computer for free**
When I want to try out or review a piece of software, I want to install and run my own copy on my computer with only free tools and no outside accounts or services, so I can evaluate it without paying or signing up for anything.
- Role: Host

**J18. Run it on my own server**
When I want my friends to use a tool for real, I want to run it on a server I control, without depending on any third-party company's services, so I can keep it running and keep our data with us.
- Role: Host

**J19. Get proof that it works**
When I evaluate a piece of software, I want quick, repeatable proof that it behaves as described in the common web browsers, so I can trust its claims without checking everything by hand.
- Role: Host
