# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

content.content:
80:- **Results:** totals appear when the user presses **Calculate**. Changing any input hides the old result until Calculate is pressed again.
97:3. **Tip:** a % or an amount. Tip may be 0. For a % tip, each bill has a "tip on" option: **items only (default)** or **items + tax**. Neither option includes other charges: a tip is never calculated on other charges.
106:   - Each group bill has one payer, and **the payer must be one of that bill's participants**. The payer list only offers ticked participants. If the payer is unticked, Calculate and Save show "The payer must be one of the people on this bill".
163:  - After Calculate, the page scrolls down to them.
165:  - Before the first Calculate, the area reads "Press Calculate to see results".
206:- [ ] Given I press Calculate with valid inputs, then the results appear below the form and the page scrolls to them. Given I change any input, then the results area goes back to "Press Calculate to see results".
215:- [ ] Given I use only the keyboard, then I can sign up, create a group, add a bill, calculate, save and record a settle-up, with a visible focus outline at every step.
234:- [ ] Given items 12.50 and 7.50, tax 10%, other charges blank, tip 15% on items, when I press Calculate, then subtotal 20.00, tax 2.00, other charges 0.00, tip 3.00 and total 25.00 are shown.
235:- [ ] Given items 12.50 and 7.50, tax 10%, other charges 5%, tip 15% on items, when I press Calculate, then subtotal 20.00, tax 2.00, other charges 1.00, tip 3.00 and total 26.00 are shown.
243:- [ ] Given no items, when I press Calculate, then I see "Add at least one item" and no result.
247:- [ ] Given 0 participants selected, when I press Calculate, then I see "Choose who took part" and no result (no division by zero).
260:- [ ] Given an item with nobody ticked, when I press Calculate, then I see "Choose who shared this item" and no result.
268:- [ ] Given Omar is chosen as payer and then unticked as a participant, when I press Calculate or Save, then I see "The payer must be one of the people on this bill" and nothing is saved.
308:- [ ] Given I switch other charges between % and amount after a result is showing, then the old result is hidden until I press Calculate again.
309:- [ ] Given an error is showing, when I fix the field and press Calculate, then the error clears and the correct result appears, with no reload needed.
310:- [ ] Given a result is showing, when I change any input, then the old result is hidden until I press Calculate again.
313:- [ ] Given any bill (solo, equal or itemized) with no items, when I press Calculate, then I see "Add at least one item" and no result.
315:- [ ] Given 200 items of 1,000,000.00, tax 100%, other charges 100% and tip 100% on items + tax, when I press Calculate, then the grand total is exactly 1,000,000,000.00.
324:- [ ] Given a saved bill (solo or group) with other charges, when I reopen it, then the other-charges value and its % / amount setting are shown exactly as saved, and editing them recalculates the total (and group balances).

content.content:
### US-05 Total a solo bill
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to enter my bill's items, tax, other charges and tip and see the exact total, **so that** I pay the right amount.
- **Job:** J1 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given items 12.50 and 7.50, tax 10%, other charges blank and tip 15% on items, when I press Calculate, then I see subtotal 20.00, tax 2.00, other charges 0.00, tip 3.00 and total 25.00.
2. Given items 12.50 and 7.50, tax 10%, other charges 5% and tip 15% on items, when I press Calculate, then I see subtotal 20.00, tax 2.00, other charges 1.00, tip 3.00 and total 26.00.
3. Given an items subtotal of 100.00, tax 10.00 (amount), other charges blank and tip 15% on items + tax, when I press Calculate, then the tip is 16.50 and the total is 126.50.
4. Given an items subtotal of 100.00, tax 10.00 (amount), other charges 7.50 (amount) and tip 15% on items + tax, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 7.50, the tip is 16.50 (other charges are not tipped on), and the total is 134.00.
5. Given an items subtotal of 100.00, tax 10% and other charges 10%, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 10.00 (a % of the items only, not of items + tax).
6. Given an items subtotal of 33.33 and other charges 12.5%, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 4.17 (4.16625 rounded half-up).
7. Given an items subtotal of 20.00 and tip 12.5%, then the tip is 2.50. Given an items subtotal of 20.00 and tax 8.25%, then the tax is 1.65.
8. Given an items subtotal of 0.01 and other charges 5%, then other charges is 0.00 (rounded half-up) and no error is shown.
9. Given other charges 0 or 0.00, then it's treated as "no other charges", shows 0.00, and causes no error.
10. Given tip 0, then the tip shows 0.00 with no error.
11. Given a new bill, then the "tip on" option starts at items only.
12. Given an items subtotal of 0.01, tax 0, other charges 1,000,000.00 (amount) and tip 0, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 1,000,000.00 and the total is 1,000,000.01.
13. Given no items, when I press Calculate, then I see "Add at least one item" and no result.
14. Given any invalid field (see US-25), when I press Calculate, then no result is shown.
15. Given an empty tax box, when I type 5, then the box shows "5" (not "05"), and a tax left blank counts as 0.


### US-06 Choose the currency of a solo bill
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to pick the currency symbol for my bill, **so that** amounts are shown the way I paid them.
- **Job:** J15 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a new solo bill, when I open the currency picker, then it offers exactly $, €, £, ¥, ₹, Rs, PKR, ₩, ₺, R$, CHF, AED, SAR and "Other", with PKR in capitals.
2. Given I pick a symbol from the list, then every amount on the bill is shown with that symbol, and no currency conversion happens.
3. Given I pick "Other" and type "kr" or "zł", then every amount is shown with that symbol.
4. Given "Other" with a blank symbol, a symbol of 4+ characters (e.g. "abcd") or one containing a digit (e.g. "R1"), when I press Calculate or Save, then I see "Enter a currency symbol of up to 3 characters, with no digits" and nothing is saved.
5. Given "Other" with " kr " (spaces around it), then it's saved as "kr".
6. Given an unsaved bill, I can change its currency freely.
7. Given the bill has been saved once, when I edit it, then the currency can't be changed.
8. Given an invalid currency symbol is sent straight to the server, then it's rejected and nothing is saved.


### US-07 Save a solo bill to my history
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to save a bill and see it in my history, **so that** I have a record of what I spent.
- **Job:** J2 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a valid solo bill, when I save it, then it appears at the top of my history (newest first) showing its name, date, currency and total.
2. Given I leave the name empty, when I save, then the bill is named "Bill – date" (using the bill's date).
3. Given a bill name of exactly 60 characters, then it's accepted. A name of 61 or more characters shows a clear message and the bill isn't saved.
4. Given the bill has an invalid field (see US-25), when I press Save, then the field's message is shown and nothing is saved.
5. Given I have several saved bills, then my history lists them newest first, and shows only my own bills.


### US-08 Open, edit and delete saved solo bills
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to reopen, fix or remove a saved bill, **so that** my record stays accurate.
- **Job:** J2 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a saved solo bill, when I open it, then every input and result is shown exactly as saved, including other charges and its % / amount setting, and the "tip on" setting.
2. Given I change an amount and save, then the totals are recalculated and checked with the same rules as a new bill. Invalid edits show the same messages and aren't saved.
3. Given I edit other charges (value or % / amount), when I save, then the total is recalculated to match.
4. Given I'm editing a saved bill, then its currency can't be changed.
5. Given I press Delete, then I'm asked to confirm. Cancel keeps the bill unchanged, and Confirm removes it from my history.


### US-13 Record an equal-split group bill
**As a** Group member, **I want** to record a group bill split evenly between the people who took part, **so that** each pays an equal share that adds up exactly to the bill.
- **Job:** J3 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a group of 10 members, when I add a bill with 5 participants, paid by one of them, then only those 5 are charged and the other 5 members' balances don't change.
2. Given a grand total of 100.00 and 3 participants, when I press Calculate, then the shares are 33.34 / 33.33 / 33.33, the first participant in list order is marked as paying the extra cent, and the shares add up to 100.00.
3. Given an items subtotal of 90.00, tax 0, other charges 10% and tip 0, split between 3 participants, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 9.00, the grand total is 99.00, and each share is 33.00.
4. Given an items subtotal of 10.00 and other charges 0.01 (amount), split between 2 participants, then the grand total is 10.01 and the shares are 5.01 and 5.00.
5. Given a grand total of 0.01 split between 2 participants, then the shares are 0.01 and 0.00.
6. Given an items subtotal of 1,000,000.00, tax 0, other charges blank and a 100% tip on items, split between 50 participants, then the grand total is 2,000,000.00, each share is 40,000.00, and the shares add up to the total.
7. Given an items subtotal of 1,000,000.00, tax 0, other charges 1,000,000.00 (amount) and tip 0, split between 3 participants, then the grand total is 2,000,000.00 and the shares are 666,666.67 / 666,666.67 / 666,666.66.
8. Given no participants are selected, when I press Calculate, then I see "Choose who took part" and no result (no division by zero).
9. Given no items, when I press Calculate, then I see "Add at least one item" and no result.
10. Given an equal-split bill, then tax, other charges and tip follow the shared rules above, including the "tip on" option.


### US-14 Record an itemized group bill
**As a** Group member, **I want** to record which items each person had, including shared dishes, **so that** everyone pays for what they had plus a fair part of tax, other charges and tip.
- **Job:** J4 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given Ali has a 40.00 steak and Sara a 10.00 salad, with tax 5.00, other charges blank and tip 10.00, when I press Calculate, then Ali's share is 52.00 and Sara's is 13.00.
2. Given the same bill with other charges 2.50 (amount), then Ali pays 2.00 and Sara 0.50 of the other charges, Ali's share is 54.00, Sara's is 13.50, and they add up to the grand total of 67.50.
3. Given 12.00 nachos ticked for Ali, Sara and Omar, then each is charged 4.00 for the nachos.
4. Given a 10.00 item shared by 3 people, then their parts are 3.34 / 3.33 / 3.33, with the extra cent going to the first ticked person.
5. Given three participants with 10.00 of items each and other charges 0.10, then their other-charges parts are 0.04 / 0.03 / 0.03: the leftover cent goes to the first participant in list order when there's a tie.
6. Given any itemized bill, then tax, other charges and tip are each split separately in proportion to each participant's items subtotal (leftover cents by largest remainder). Each of those parts adds up exactly to the bill's tax, other charges and tip.
7. Given a participant with no items, and other charges of 5.00 on the bill, then that participant's other-charges part is 0.00, and they owe 0.00 in total (items, tax, other charges and tip).
8. Given an item with nobody ticked, when I press Calculate, then I see "Choose who shared this item" next to it and no result.
9. Given any valid itemized bill, then the per-person totals add up exactly to the grand total.
10. Given an item row, when I open its people dropdown, then it lists only this bill's participants, each with a tick box, and I can tick one or several.
11. Given I've ticked Ali, Sara and Omar for an item and closed the dropdown, then the row shows "Ali, Sara, Omar".
12. Given I untick a participant from the bill, then they disappear from every item's dropdown, and items left with nobody ticked show "Choose who shared this item" when I press Calculate.


### US-15 Record who paid a group bill
**As a** Group member, **I want** to record which participant paid the bill, **so that** they're credited and the others owe them.
- **Job:** J5 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a bill's participants are Ali and Sara, then the payer list offers only Ali and Sara.
2. Given Omar is chosen as payer and then unticked as a participant, when I press Calculate or Save, then I see "The payer must be one of the people on this bill" and nothing is saved.
3. Given Ali paid 65.00 and the shares are Ali 52.00 and Sara 13.00, then Ali's balance goes up by 13.00 (65.00 paid − his own 52.00 share) and Sara's goes down by 13.00.
4. Given any bill, then exactly one payer is recorded. There is no option for several payers.
5. Given a removed member, then they're never offered as payer or participant on a new bill.


### US-18 Edit and delete group bills and settle-ups
**As a** Group member, **I want** to correct or remove any group bill or settle-up, **so that** our balances stay right.
- **Job:** J6 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given any current member, then they can edit or delete any bill or settle-up in the group, not just their own.
2. Given I edit a bill or settle-up and save, then it's checked with the same rules as a new one, and the balances update.
3. Given I reopen a group bill with other charges, then its value and % / amount setting are shown exactly as saved, and editing them recalculates the bill and the balances.
4. Given I press Delete on a bill, then I'm asked to confirm. Cancel keeps it, and Confirm removes it and updates the balances.
5. Given a bill or settle-up that includes a removed member, when I try to edit or delete it, then I see "Restore Omar to change this bill" and nothing changes. A message about Delete shows at the top of the page, next to the Delete button.

### US-05 Total a solo bill
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to enter my bill's items, tax, other charges and tip and see the exact total, **so that** I pay the right amount.
- **Job:** J1 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given items 12.50 and 7.50, tax 10%, other charges blank and tip 15% on items, when I press Calculate, then I see subtotal 20.00, tax 2.00, other charges 0.00, tip 3.00 and total 25.00.
2. Given items 12.50 and 7.50, tax 10%, other charges 5% and tip 15% on items, when I press Calculate, then I see subtotal 20.00, tax 2.00, other charges 1.00, tip 3.00 and total 26.00.
3. Given an items subtotal of 100.00, tax 10.00 (amount), other charges blank and tip 15% on items + tax, when I press Calculate, then the tip is 16.50 and the total is 126.50.
4. Given an items subtotal of 100.00, tax 10.00 (amount), other charges 7.50 (amount) and tip 15% on items + tax, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 7.50, the tip is 16.50 (other charges are not tipped on), and the total is 134.00.
5. Given an items subtotal of 100.00, tax 10% and other charges 10%, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 10.00 (a % of the items only, not of items + tax).
6. Given an items subtotal of 33.33 and other charges 12.5%, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 4.17 (4.16625 rounded half-up).
7. Given an items subtotal of 20.00 and tip 12.5%, then the tip is 2.50. Given an items subtotal of 20.00 and tax 8.25%, then the tax is 1.65.
8. Given an items subtotal of 0.01 and other charges 5%, then other charges is 0.00 (rounded half-up) and no error is shown.
9. Given other charges 0 or 0.00, then it's treated as "no other charges", shows 0.00, and causes no error.
10. Given tip 0, then the tip shows 0.00 with no error.
11. Given a new bill, then the "tip on" option starts at items only.
12. Given an items subtotal of 0.01, tax 0, other charges 1,000,000.00 (amount) and tip 0, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 1,000,000.00 and the total is 1,000,000.01.
13. Given no items, when I press Calculate, then I see "Add at least one item" and no result.
14. Given any invalid field (see US-25), when I press Calculate, then no result is shown.
15. Given an empty tax box, when I type 5, then the box shows "5" (not "05"), and a tax left blank counts as 0.


### US-06 Choose the currency of a solo bill
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to pick the currency symbol for my bill, **so that** amounts are shown the way I paid them.
- **Job:** J15 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a new solo bill, when I open the currency picker, then it offers exactly $, €, £, ¥, ₹, Rs, PKR, ₩, ₺, R$, CHF, AED, SAR and "Other", with PKR in capitals.
2. Given I pick a symbol from the list, then every amount on the bill is shown with that symbol, and no currency conversion happens.
3. Given I pick "Other" and type "kr" or "zł", then every amount is shown with that symbol.
4. Given "Other" with a blank symbol, a symbol of 4+ characters (e.g. "abcd") or one containing a digit (e.g. "R1"), when I press Calculate or Save, then I see "Enter a currency symbol of up to 3 characters, with no digits" and nothing is saved.
5. Given "Other" with " kr " (spaces around it), then it's saved as "kr".
6. Given an unsaved bill, I can change its currency freely.
7. Given the bill has been saved once, when I edit it, then the currency can't be changed.
8. Given an invalid currency symbol is sent straight to the server, then it's rejected and nothing is saved.


### US-07 Save a solo bill to my history
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to save a bill and see it in my history, **so that** I have a record of what I spent.
- **Job:** J2 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a valid solo bill, when I save it, then it appears at the top of my history (newest first) showing its name, date, currency and total.
2. Given I leave the name empty, when I save, then the bill is named "Bill – date" (using the bill's date).
3. Given a bill name of exactly 60 characters, then it's accepted. A name of 61 or more characters shows a clear message and the bill isn't saved.
4. Given the bill has an invalid field (see US-25), when I press Save, then the field's message is shown and nothing is saved.
5. Given I have several saved bills, then my history lists them newest first, and shows only my own bills.


### US-08 Open, edit and delete saved solo bills
**As a** Solo diner, **I want** to reopen, fix or remove a saved bill, **so that** my record stays accurate.
- **Job:** J2 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a saved solo bill, when I open it, then every input and result is shown exactly as saved, including other charges and its % / amount setting, and the "tip on" setting.
2. Given I change an amount and save, then the totals are recalculated and checked with the same rules as a new bill. Invalid edits show the same messages and aren't saved.
3. Given I edit other charges (value or % / amount), when I save, then the total is recalculated to match.
4. Given I'm editing a saved bill, then its currency can't be changed.
5. Given I press Delete, then I'm asked to confirm. Cancel keeps the bill unchanged, and Confirm removes it from my history.


### US-13 Record an equal-split group bill
**As a** Group member, **I want** to record a group bill split evenly between the people who took part, **so that** each pays an equal share that adds up exactly to the bill.
- **Job:** J3 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a group of 10 members, when I add a bill with 5 participants, paid by one of them, then only those 5 are charged and the other 5 members' balances don't change.
2. Given a grand total of 100.00 and 3 participants, when I press Calculate, then the shares are 33.34 / 33.33 / 33.33, the first participant in list order is marked as paying the extra cent, and the shares add up to 100.00.
3. Given an items subtotal of 90.00, tax 0, other charges 10% and tip 0, split between 3 participants, when I press Calculate, then other charges is 9.00, the grand total is 99.00, and each share is 33.00.
4. Given an items subtotal of 10.00 and other charges 0.01 (amount), split between 2 participants, then the grand total is 10.01 and the shares are 5.01 and 5.00.
5. Given a grand total of 0.01 split between 2 participants, then the shares are 0.01 and 0.00.
6. Given an items subtotal of 1,000,000.00, tax 0, other charges blank and a 100% tip on items, split between 50 participants, then the grand total is 2,000,000.00, each share is 40,000.00, and the shares add up to the total.
7. Given an items subtotal of 1,000,000.00, tax 0, other charges 1,000,000.00 (amount) and tip 0, split between 3 participants, then the grand total is 2,000,000.00 and the shares are 666,666.67 / 666,666.67 / 666,666.66.
8. Given no participants are selected, when I press Calculate, then I see "Choose who took part" and no result (no division by zero).
9. Given no items, when I press Calculate, then I see "Add at least one item" and no result.
10. Given an equal-split bill, then tax, other charges and tip follow the shared rules above, including the "tip on" option.


### US-14 Record an itemized group bill
**As a** Group member, **I want** to record which items each person had, including shared dishes, **so that** everyone pays for what they had plus a fair part of tax, other charges and tip.
- **Job:** J4 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given Ali has a 40.00 steak and Sara a 10.00 salad, with tax 5.00, other charges blank and tip 10.00, when I press Calculate, then Ali's share is 52.00 and Sara's is 13.00.
2. Given the same bill with other charges 2.50 (amount), then Ali pays 2.00 and Sara 0.50 of the other charges, Ali's share is 54.00, Sara's is 13.50, and they add up to the grand total of 67.50.
3. Given 12.00 nachos ticked for Ali, Sara and Omar, then each is charged 4.00 for the nachos.
4. Given a 10.00 item shared by 3 people, then their parts are 3.34 / 3.33 / 3.33, with the extra cent going to the first ticked person.
5. Given three participants with 10.00 of items each and other charges 0.10, then their other-charges parts are 0.04 / 0.03 / 0.03: the leftover cent goes to the first participant in list order when there's a tie.
6. Given any itemized bill, then tax, other charges and tip are each split separately in proportion to each participant's items subtotal (leftover cents by largest remainder). Each of those parts adds up exactly to the bill's tax, other charges and tip.
7. Given a participant with no items, and other charges of 5.00 on the bill, then that participant's other-charges part is 0.00, and they owe 0.00 in total (items, tax, other charges and tip).
8. Given an item with nobody ticked, when I press Calculate, then I see "Choose who shared this item" next to it and no result.
9. Given any valid itemized bill, then the per-person totals add up exactly to the grand total.
10. Given an item row, when I open its people dropdown, then it lists only this bill's participants, each with a tick box, and I can tick one or several.
11. Given I've ticked Ali, Sara and Omar for an item and closed the dropdown, then the row shows "Ali, Sara, Omar".
12. Given I untick a participant from the bill, then they disappear from every item's dropdown, and items left with nobody ticked show "Choose who shared this item" when I press Calculate.


### US-15 Record who paid a group bill
**As a** Group member, **I want** to record which participant paid the bill, **so that** they're credited and the others owe them.
- **Job:** J5 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given a bill's participants are Ali and Sara, then the payer list offers only Ali and Sara.
2. Given Omar is chosen as payer and then unticked as a participant, when I press Calculate or Save, then I see "The payer must be one of the people on this bill" and nothing is saved.
3. Given Ali paid 65.00 and the shares are Ali 52.00 and Sara 13.00, then Ali's balance goes up by 13.00 (65.00 paid − his own 52.00 share) and Sara's goes down by 13.00.
4. Given any bill, then exactly one payer is recorded. There is no option for several payers.
5. Given a removed member, then they're never offered as payer or participant on a new bill.


### US-18 Edit and delete group bills and settle-ups
**As a** Group member, **I want** to correct or remove any group bill or settle-up, **so that** our balances stay right.
- **Job:** J6 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given any current member, then they can edit or delete any bill or settle-up in the group, not just their own.
2. Given I edit a bill or settle-up and save, then it's checked with the same rules as a new one, and the balances update.
3. Given I reopen a group bill with other charges, then its value and % / amount setting are shown exactly as saved, and editing them recalculates the bill and the balances.
4. Given I press Delete on a bill, then I'm asked to confirm. Cancel keeps it, and Confirm removes it and updates the balances.
5. Given a bill or settle-up that includes a removed member, when I try to edit or delete it, then I see "Restore Omar to change this bill" and nothing changes. A message about Delete shows at the top of the page, next to the Delete button.

### US-26 Carry on safely after a result or an error
**As a** Solo diner or Group member, **I want** results and errors to update correctly as I keep working, **so that** I never act on an out-of-date figure.
- **Job:** J14 · **Status:** Implemented

Acceptance criteria:
1. Given an error is showing, when I fix the field and press Calculate, then the error disappears and the correct result appears, with no page reload needed.
2. Given a result is showing, when I change any input, then the old result is hidden until I press Calculate again.
3. Given a result is showing, when I switch tax, tip or other charges between % and amount, or change the "tip on" option, then the old result is hidden until I press Calculate again.
4. Given I press Calculate several times without changing anything, then the same result is shown each time.
5. Given a new bill form, then the results area below the form reads "Press Calculate to see results".
6. Given valid inputs, when I press Calculate, then the results appear below the form, on every screen size, and the page scrolls down to them.
7. Given results are showing, when I change any input, then the results area goes back to "Press Calculate to see results".
8. Given a bill in Rs with a total of 1234567.5 and a share of 400, then the results show "Rs 1,234,567.50" and "Rs 400.00". In $ they show "$1,234,567.50" and "$400.00".
9. Given a field is showing an error, when I edit that field, then its error disappears straight away, before I press Calculate.
10. Given results are showing, then each % line shows its rate, e.g. "Tax (5%)", "Other charges (10%)", "Tip (15% of items)" or "Tip (15% of items + tax)".
11. Given a bill form, then the "Save bill" button sits under the results, with any message about saving just above it. When the server rejects a field, the cursor moves to that field.


### US-39 Edit a group's name and currency
**As a** Group member, **I want** to rename a group or change its currency, **so that** I can fix a mistake or follow a change of plan.
- **Job:** J6 · **Status:** Implemented

input.prompt:
Review a UX redesign of the bill screens in a self-hosted bill-splitting web app (React 19 + react-router 7, Express 5, Postgres). Project root: /Users/sanaarshad/Desktop/Sana-Arshad-calculator; code under src/. READ-ONLY: do not edit files, do not run Playwright or vitest (other agents are running tests), do not start servers. You may read, grep, and run `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and `npx eslint client` from src/. `git diff HEAD -- src/client docs` shows the changes; new untracked files: src/client/components/CurrencyNote.tsx, src/tests/unit/billEditor.test.ts. src/client/components/PeoplePicker.tsx was deleted.

What the user asked for: better UX on the group "add bill" page and across the app; fix dropdown padding; after saving a bill go to where it is listed; make adding items, tax and other charges less of a hassle; saved bills open read-only with an Edit button; better wording for a saved solo bill's fixed currency; an info button explaining the group currency is only a symbol (no conversion; changing it relabels every bill). They chose to KEEP the Calculate button (no live totals).

What was built (please verify correctness, accessibility and edge cases):
- src/client/components/BillForm.tsx (rewritten): People section (checkbox chips + "Everyone" toggle button with aria-pressed; "Who paid" select; split radios styled as a segmented switch with a visually-hidden "(each pays for what they had)"); items as rows with visually-hidden labels, icon "Remove item N" buttons, Enter-key navigation (name → price → next row / add row; isComposing guarded) and focus management via a focusItem state + effect; per-item sharer chips with "Everyone"; charges as fieldsets with visually-hidden legends ("Other charges (optional)"), a % / currency-symbol radio switch that focuses the input on pointerup (keyboard arrow use unaffected).
- src/client/billEditor.ts: fully empty item rows are dropped from toBillInput/toGroupBillInput; toFormErrors maps item error keys back to form positions (client and server errors); rateLabels hides 0%; revealResults uses block 'nearest'.
- src/client/components/Results.tsx: optional title/items for the read-only receipt; the aria-live line only while editing.
- src/client/pages/SoloPages.tsx and GroupBillPages.tsx: read-only view pages (SoloBillViewPage, GroupBillViewPage) with Edit/Delete; editor pages for /new and /:id/edit; a side column (Calculate as `<button type="submit" form={formId}>` outside the form, Results, Save); after save `navigate(list, { replace: true, state: { savedBillId } })`; locked group bills redirect from /edit to the view.
- src/client/hooks.ts useSavedBillId; lists (SoloListPage, GroupPage BillsTab) mark the saved row.
- src/client/components/CurrencyNote.tsx: disclosure button + note; used on the group page and group bill editor.
- src/client/styles.css: custom select chevron via CSS variables (light/dark), chips (invisible full-size input covering the chip; :has() states), bill layout grid (two columns >=1180px, sticky side), item rows, charges grid, receipt items, saved-row badge, info button/note.
- src/client/main.tsx routes.
- docs/user-stories.md criteria updated (US-05 #16/#17, US-06 #7, US-07 #1, US-08, US-13 #11/#12, US-14 #10-#12, US-18 #2/#3/#5, US-26 #5/#6/#10, US-39 #5).

Look especially for: React state/effect bugs (stale closures in onItemKey/addItem, focus effect loops), the form attribute + implicit submission (Enter in non-item fields must still Calculate), toFormErrors edge cases, the unsaved-changes guard on the new routes (Cancel, save navigation with replace), the "Everyone" behaviour with zero people, a11y (fieldset/legend names, aria-pressed chips, focus-visible on chips, contrast of the tick icon in dark mode, 24x24 target sizes), CSS specificity clashes (e.g. older .badge/.seg/.check rules overriding new ones), mobile layout at 360px, and whether the docs now match the behaviour exactly. Output: findings with severity (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), file:line, concrete failure scenario and a minimal fix; end with APPROVE or REQUEST CHANGES (only for HIGH/MEDIUM you can make concrete).

The redesign is built, but the browser tests haven't passed yet. Three test helpers are updating them, a reviewer is checking the code, and the full test suite will run twice once they finish. Nothing is committed.

What changed:

- **Saved bills open read-only.** Clicking a saved bill shows it as a receipt: each item, the totals with their rates, who paid and each person's share. It has "Edit bill" and "Delete" buttons. Editing has its own page with a Cancel button. A group bill that includes a removed member has no Edit button.
- **After saving**, a new or edited bill takes you back to its list, where it's highlighted and marked "Saved".
- **Adding items is faster.** Pressing Enter moves from an item's name to its price, then to the next item, adding a new line after the last. A spare empty line is simply ignored. Each item has a small × to remove it.
- **Tax, other charges and tip** each sit on one line. The switch shows "%" or your currency symbol (for example "Rs") instead of the word "Amount", and tapping it puts the cursor straight in the box.
- **Group bills:**
  - People are tap-to-toggle name chips, with an "Everyone" option.
  - "How to split" is a two-button switch with a line explaining each option.
  - When splitting by items, each item has its own row of name chips instead of a dropdown.
  - On a computer, Calculate, the results and Save bill sit beside the form; on a phone they sit below it.
- **The Calculate button stays**, as you chose. Results still appear only after you press it.
- **Dropdowns** now have even padding, with the arrow sitting properly inside the box.
- **Currency:**
  - Saved solo bills now say: "A saved bill keeps its currency. To use a different one, delete this bill and add it again with the right currency."
  - On the group page and the add-bill page, "Currency: Rs" has a small ⓘ button explaining it's only a symbol: nothing is converted, and changing it relabels every bill in the group.

One small extra: "Tax (0%)" no longer shows on bills that have no tax.

The user stories in the docs now describe all of this. I'll report back once the tests pass and the review is done.

## 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

## 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## 4076911a-8223-48b7-bd8d-6725c8583dad
This is an MCP server provided by Gmail API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Gmail.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.
</system-reminder>

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. There are different types of agents that you can launch, with each type having specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Agent types which you are able to launch were given to you in a message from the system at the start of the conversation, and are supplied again if the list of available agents changes.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to choose which type of agent you want to launch. A type of "fork" forks yourself, allowing the fork to inherit your full conversation and context, and ensuring that it runs on the same model that you are running on (a `model` override is ignored for forks). For other types of subagents, they start fresh without your context window. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

There are pros and cons of delegating your work to subagents. Below we'll outline some of them to help you use your best judgement with this powerful tool.

The largest benefit in delegating to subagents is that it allows you to parallelize your work. For instance, if there is work that needs to be done by an intelligent agent such as yourself, but across (for example) several or ten or even one hundred instances of something (sets of data, parts of a codebase, servers, anything), you may want to use subagents for this work. In this case you'd want to ensure the work truly needs your intelligence, rather than being something overly simple or rote which could be done by a static script or short program. In this case your work can be significantly sped up by spinning up many agents to help you out.

The other benefit of delegation is to help you stay focused on the primary task at hand. Sometimes you will have tasks that feel like a side quest, which are not blocking you, but might help you gain some information you'd want in the future as you go about working on your primary task. For example, maybe some section of the codebase which you are not actively working on should be refactored, or maybe you want to do data analysis or set up a service which you think you'll need later, or you want to perform some important checks in the background. These are reasonable things you can outsource to a subagent so that you can remain focused on your primary task. It can be useful to think of yourself as an operator in this sense - you have entire teams of potential agents available to you all of whom are eager to help you out when you need it, and you should thus use them intelligently.

The cons of delegation are that the subagents which you launch, with the exception of a fork, only have the context that you give them. This might mean that the subagent is missing a lot of context which would help it make better decisions or produce more useful results. For this reason, when using non-fork subagents, you should provide to it as much context as possible to help it perform well. You don't have to limit the prompt to text you write yourself; you can also point subagents at any relevant documents or files whose location you know that you think would be helpful. You should make the scope clear (and generally the scope should be relatively narrow), while at the same time treating the subagent respectfully and as an intellectual peer (they are often the same model as you, just missing some context). More context and more 'why' is generally always better to provide to other agents, because this gives them more information they can use to help them exercise strong judgement, and therefore help you succeed at your task as well. Teamwork!

The other challenge of subagent usage is that you have less observability into what is happening compared to your own work, where you have full visibility into every single tool call, result, and action that occurs. Subagents run in the background, but you will be notified when one completes. If you don't yet have the results from a subagent that you launched, it is likely still running, so be sure to keep that in mind and not make up results from subagents which haven't yet finished their tasks. The subagent's final report which is given back to you when it has finished is not shown to the user - it is just shown to you, so if you want to relay something from it which is important, you have to do that yourself.

You can use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously-spawned agent with its context still intact, whereas a new Agent call starts fresh (except for fork types, which inherit your context).

Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`). Also take note that `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

In conclusion, it is best to use subagents for parallelizing your intelligence, for saving time, and for completing side-quests which do not block the main goal that you're actively working on. It is best to provide them with broad amounts of high-level context as well as their specific goals when you do use them. If the amount of work to be done is small (for example, just making a few file reads or searches or tool calls), that is probably not enough to warrant using a subagent.

For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. And once you've delegated a search, wait for the result to return rather than also running it yourself.
